944	   **Wave-close heartbeat (#2410):** after spot-checks finish (pass or fail),
945	   before the `## Wave {N} Complete` summary, emit as a literal line:
946	
947	   ```
948	   [checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} complete, {P}/{Q} plans done ({wave_success}/{wave_plan_count} ok)
949	   ```
950	
951	   For each SUMMARY.md:
952	   - Verify first 2 files from `key-files.created` exist on disk
953	   - Check `git log --oneline --all --grep="{phase}-{plan}"` returns ≥1 commit
954	   - Check for `## Self-Check: FAILED` marker
955	
956	   If ANY spot-check fails: report which plan failed, route to failure handler — ask "Retry plan?" or "Continue with remaining waves?"
957	
958	   If pass:
959	
960	   ```
961	   ---
962	   ## Wave {N} Complete
963	
964	   **{Plan ID}: {Plan Name}**
965	   {What was built — from SUMMARY.md}
966	   {Notable deviations, if any}
967	
968	   {If more waves: what this enables for next wave}
969	   ---
970	   ```
971	
972	7. **Handle failures:**
973	   **Step 7.0 — classify before branching (#3095):**
974	   ```bash
975	   CLASS_JSON=$(gsd_run query agent.classify-failure -- "$AGENT_RETURN_BODY")
976	   CLASS=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.class')
977	   SENTINEL=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.sentinel // empty')
978	   RETRY_AFTER=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.retryAfterSeconds // empty')
979	   if [ -n "$RETRY_AFTER" ]; then RETRY_HINT="  Provider hinted retry-after: ${RETRY_AFTER}s"; else RETRY_HINT=""; fi
980	   ```
981	   One classifier branch handles sentinels across Claude/Copilot/Codex/Gemini. Reference: `docs/research/provider-rate-limit-signals.md`.
982	   **Step 7.1 — `class == "quota-exceeded"`:**
983	   Do not offer "retry now". Run step-5 spot-check first; if SUMMARY.md is missing but commits exist, route to safe-resume (`state.verify-against-disk`) instead of immediate redispatch.
984	   ```text
985	   ⚠ Plan {plan_id} terminated by provider quota / rate limit
986	     Runtime sentinel: {SENTINEL}
987	     {RETRY_HINT}
988	     Partial commits on worktree branch: {N}
989	     SUMMARY.md present: {yes|no}
990	     1. Wait for quota reset, then resume (recommended)
991	   2. Switch to a different runtime / model and resume
992	   3. Abort phase and report partial state
993	   ```
994	   Re-run `/gsd-execute-phase` after quota reset for Option 1.
995	   **Step 7.2 — `class == "classify-handoff-bug"`:**
996	   If error contains `classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined`, treat as Claude runtime bug. Run the same step-5 spot-checks; PASS => treat as success, FAIL => fall through.
997	   **Step 7.3 — `class == "unknown-failure"`:**
998	   Report failed plan and ask Continue/Stop; continuing may cascade into dependent plan failures.
999	
1000	7b. **Pre-wave dependency check (waves 2+ only):**
1001	Before wave N+1, run `gsd-tools.cjs query verify.key-links {phase_dir}/{plan}-PLAN.md` for each upcoming plan.
1002	If any PRIOR-wave artifact link fails, present: - `## Cross-Plan Wiring Gap` with plan/link/from/pattern rows - Options: investigate+fix before continue, or continue with cascade risk
1003	Skip key-links that reference files in the CURRENT (upcoming) wave. 8. **Execute checkpoint plans between waves** — see `<checkpoint_handling>`. 9. **Proceed to next wave.**
1004	</step>
1005	<step name="checkpoint_handling">
1006	Plans with `autonomous: false` require user interaction.
1007	**Auto-mode checkpoint handling:**
1008	Read auto-advance config (chain flag OR user preference — same boolean as `check.auto-mode`):
1009	
1010	```bash
1011	AUTO_MODE=$(gsd_run query check auto-mode --pick active 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
1012	```
1013	
1014	When executor returns a checkpoint AND `AUTO_MODE` is `true`:
1015	
1016	- **human-verify** → Auto-spawn continuation agent with `{user_response}` = `"approved"`. Log `⚡ Auto-approved checkpoint`.
1017	- **decision** → Auto-spawn continuation agent with `{user_response}` = first option from checkpoint details. Log `⚡ Auto-selected: [option]`.
1018	- **human-action** → Present to user (existing behavior below). Auth gates cannot be automated.
1019	
1020	**Standard flow (not auto-mode, or human-action type):**
1021	
1022	1. Spawn agent for checkpoint plan
1023	2. Agent runs until checkpoint task or auth gate → returns structured state
1024	3. Agent return includes: completed tasks table, current task + blocker, checkpoint type/details, what's awaited
1025	4. **Present to user:**
1026	
1027	   ```
1028	   ## Checkpoint: [Type]
1029	
1030	   **Plan:** 03-03 Dashboard Layout
1031	   **Progress:** 2/3 tasks complete
1032	
1033	   [Checkpoint Details from agent return]
1034	   [Awaiting section from agent return]
1035	   ```
1036	
1037	5. User responds: "approved"/"done" | issue description | decision selection
1038	6. **Spawn continuation agent (NOT resume)** using continuation-prompt.md template:
1039	   - `{completed_tasks_table}`: From checkpoint return
1040	   - `{resume_task_number}` + `{resume_task_name}`: Current task
1041	   - `{user_response}`: What user provided
1042	   - `{resume_instructions}`: Based on checkpoint type
1043	7. Continuation agent verifies previous commits, continues from resume point
1044	8. Repeat until plan completes or user stops
1045	
1046	**Why fresh agent, not resume:** Resume relies on internal serialization that breaks with parallel tool calls. Fresh agents with explicit state are more reliable.
1047	
1048	**Checkpoints in parallel waves:** Agent pauses and returns while other parallel agents may complete. Present checkpoint, spawn continuation, wait for all before next wave.
1049	</step>

1120	   - RED gate: A failing test commit exists (`test(...)` commit with MUST-fail evidence)
1121	   - GREEN gate: An implementation commit exists (`feat(...)` commit making tests pass)
1122	   - REFACTOR gate: Optional cleanup commit (`refactor(...)` commit, tests still pass)

1136

1139	   | {id} |  ✓  |   ✓   |    ✓     | Pass   |
1140	   | {id} |  ✓  |   ✗   |    —     | FAIL   |

1143	**Escalation under MVP+TDD.** When `MVP_MODE=true` AND `TDD_MODE=true`, the review verdict escalates from advisory to **blocking**: missing RED or GREEN gate commits prevent marking the phase complete.

1151	`--force-mvp-gate` is the escape hatch (documented, not yet implemented). Policy is:
1152	
1153	- `MVP_MODE=true` AND `TDD_MODE=true`: violations are **blocking** unless explicitly overridden.
1154	- otherwise: violations are advisory/non-blocking and are surfaced for review.

Route via `gsd-tools.cjs query agent.classify-failure` → `class: "quota-exceeded"`. Do not offer retry-now; the right action is wait-for-reset and resume.

1	# Worktree branch check (spawn-time guard)
2	
3	Canonical, fail-closed, **verify-only** guard embedded into every worktree sub-agent
4	prompt at dispatch. This is the single source of truth for the `worktree_branch_check`
5	block — do not inline a copy elsewhere. History of coordinated edits: #2924, #2015, #3174, #48.
6	
7	**Contract for orchestrators:** before dispatch, capture `EXPECTED_BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`,
8	then embed the block below into the sub-agent prompt verbatim, substituting `{EXPECTED_BASE}`
9	with that captured SHA. The sub-agent only _verifies_ and fails closed; the orchestrator
10	(the worktree lifecycle owner) performs any base recovery — the sub-agent never rewrites a
11	worktree it did not create (#48).
12	
13	<worktree_branch_check>
14	FIRST ACTION: HEAD assertion MUST run before anything else, and this block is
15	VERIFY-ONLY. Worktrees spawned by Claude Code's `isolation="worktree"` use the
16	`worktree-agent-<id>` namespace. The orchestrator owns this worktree's lifecycle;
17	a sub-agent MUST NOT hold state-correction primitives (hard-reset, update-ref,
18	force-move, index-discard) on a worktree it did not create (#48, #2924). If ANY
19	assertion below fails, HALT immediately — print the FATAL line, `exit 42`, and let
20	the orchestrator (the lifecycle owner) decide recovery. Do NOT self-recover, do NOT
21	commit.
22	
23	```bash
24	HEAD_REF=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD || echo "DETACHED")
25	ACTUAL_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
26	if [ "$HEAD_REF" = "DETACHED" ] || echo "$ACTUAL_BRANCH" | grep -Eq '^(main|master|develop|trunk|release/.*)$'; then
27	  echo "FATAL: worktree HEAD on '$ACTUAL_BRANCH' (expected worktree-agent-*); refusing to commit or self-recover via 'git update-ref' (#2924)." >&2
28	  exit 42
29	fi
30	if ! echo "$ACTUAL_BRANCH" | grep -Eq '^worktree-agent-[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$'; then
31	  echo "FATAL: worktree HEAD '$ACTUAL_BRANCH' is not in the worktree-agent-* namespace; refusing to commit (#2924)." >&2

48	Parse optional flags from $ARGUMENTS using the typed flag parser:
49	
50	```bash
51	# Parse all code-review flags into a structured IR via code-review-flags.cjs.
52	# This is the canonical flag-parsing surface — do not replicate inline bash parsing
53	# for --fix/--all/--auto here; the module handles all flag extraction and implication
54	# logic (e.g., --all and --auto imply --fix).
55	FLAGS_JSON=$(node -e "
56	  const { parseCodeReviewFlags } = require('./gsd-core/bin/lib/code-review-flags.cjs');
57	  const flags = parseCodeReviewFlags(process.argv.slice(1));
58	  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(flags));
59	" -- "$@" 2>/dev/null)
60	
61	# Extract individual flag values from the IR
62	FIX_FLAG=$(echo "$FLAGS_JSON" | node -e "process.stdout.write(String(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf-8')).fix))")
63	FIX_ALL=$(echo "$FLAGS_JSON" | node -e "process.stdout.write(String(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf-8')).all))")
64	FIX_AUTO=$(echo "$FLAGS_JSON" | node -e "process.stdout.write(String(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf-8')).auto))")
65	DEPTH_OVERRIDE=$(echo "$FLAGS_JSON" | node -e "process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf-8')).depth)")
66	FILES_OVERRIDE=$(echo "$FLAGS_JSON" | node -e "process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf-8')).files)")
67	```

130	Three-tier scoping with explicit precedence:

134	If FILES_OVERRIDE is set (from --files flag):
135	
136	```bash
137	if [ -n "$FILES_OVERRIDE" ]; then
138	  REVIEW_FILES=()
139	  REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)
140	
141	  for file_path in "${FILES_ARRAY[@]}"; do
142	    # Security: validate path is within repository (prevent path traversal)
143	    ABS_PATH=$(realpath -m "${file_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "${file_path}")
144	    if [[ "$ABS_PATH" != "$REPO_ROOT"* ]]; then
145	      echo "Error: File path outside repository, skipping: ${file_path}"
146	      continue
147	    fi
148	
149	    # Validate path exists (relative to repo root)
150	    if [ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/${file_path}" ] || [ -f "${file_path}" ]; then
151	      REVIEW_FILES+=("$file_path")
152	    else
153	      echo "Warning: File not found, skipping: ${file_path}"
154	    fi
155	  done
156	
157	  echo "File scope: ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} files from --files override"
158	fi
159	```

180	        if (!match) { process.exit(0); }
181	        const yaml = match[1];
182	        const files = [];
183	        let inSection = null;
184	        for (const line of yaml.split('\n')) {
185	          if (/^\s+created:/.test(line)) { inSection = 'created'; continue; }
186	          if (/^\s+modified:/.test(line)) { inSection = 'modified'; continue; }
187	          if (/^\s*[\w-]+:/.test(line) && !/^\s*-/.test(line)) { inSection = null; continue; }
188	          if (inSection && /^\s+-\s+(.+)/.test(line)) {
189	            let raw = line.match(/^\s+-\s+(.+)/)[1].trim();
190	            raw = raw.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '');
191	            raw = raw.replace(/\s+\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '');
192	            raw = raw.split(/\s+—\s/)[0].trim();
193	            if (/\//.test(raw) && /\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/.test(raw)) {
194	              files.push(raw);
195	            }
196	          }
197	        }
198	        if (files.length) console.log(files.join('\n'));
199	      " 2>/dev/null)
200	
201	      # Add extracted files to REVIEW_FILES array
202	      if [ -n "$EXTRACTED" ]; then
203	        while IFS= read -r file; do
204	          if [ -n "$file" ]; then
205	            REVIEW_FILES+=("$file")
206	          fi
207	        done <<< "$EXTRACTED"
208	      fi
209	    done
210	
211	    if [ ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
212	      echo "Warning: SUMMARY artifacts found but contained no file paths. Falling back to git diff."
213	    fi
214	  fi
215	fi
216	```
217	
218	**Tier 3 — Git diff fallback (per D-02):**
219	
220	If no SUMMARY.md files found OR no files extracted from them:
221	
222	```bash
223	if [ ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
224	  # Compute diff base from phase commits — fail closed if no reliable base found
225	  PHASE_COMMITS=$(git log --oneline --all --grep="${PADDED_PHASE}" --format="%H" 2>/dev/null)
226	
227	  if [ -n "$PHASE_COMMITS" ]; then
228	    DIFF_BASE=$(echo "$PHASE_COMMITS" | tail -1)^
229	
230	    # Verify the parent commit exists (first commit in repo has no parent)
231	    if ! git rev-parse "${DIFF_BASE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
232	      DIFF_BASE=$(echo "$PHASE_COMMITS" | tail -1)
233	    fi
234	
235	    # Run git diff with specific exclusions (per D-03)
236	    DIFF_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "${DIFF_BASE}..HEAD" -- . \
237	      ':!.planning/' ':!ROADMAP.md' ':!STATE.md' \
238	      ':!*-SUMMARY.md' ':!*-VERIFICATION.md' ':!*-PLAN.md' \
239	      ':!package-lock.json' ':!yarn.lock' ':!Gemfile.lock' ':!poetry.lock' 2>/dev/null)
240	
241	    while IFS= read -r file; do
242	      [ -n "$file" ] && REVIEW_FILES+=("$file")
243	    done <<< "$DIFF_FILES"
244	
245	    echo "File scope: ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} files from git diff (base: ${DIFF_BASE})"
246	  else
247	    # Fail closed — no reliable diff base found. Do not use arbitrary HEAD~N.
248	    echo "Warning: No phase commits found for '${PADDED_PHASE}'. Cannot determine reliable diff scope."
249	    echo "Use --files flag to specify files explicitly: /gsd-code-review ${PHASE_ARG} --files=file1,file2,..."
250	  fi
251	fi
252	```
253	
254	**Post-processing (all tiers):**
255	
256	1. **Apply exclusions (per D-03):** Remove paths matching planning artifacts
257	
258	```bash
259	FILTERED_FILES=()
260	for file in "${REVIEW_FILES[@]}"; do
261	  # Skip planning directory and specific artifacts
262	  if [[ "$file" == .planning/* ]] || \
263	     [[ "$file" == ROADMAP.md ]] || \
264	     [[ "$file" == STATE.md ]] || \
265	     [[ "$file" == *-SUMMARY.md ]] || \
266	     [[ "$file" == *-VERIFICATION.md ]] || \
267	     [[ "$file" == *-PLAN.md ]]; then
268	    continue
269	  fi
270	  FILTERED_FILES+=("$file")
271	done
272	REVIEW_FILES=("${FILTERED_FILES[@]}")
273	```
274	
275	2. **Filter deleted files:** Remove paths that don't exist on disk
276	
277	```bash
278	EXISTING_FILES=()
279	DELETED_COUNT=0
280	for file in "${REVIEW_FILES[@]}"; do
281	  if [ -f "$file" ]; then
282	    EXISTING_FILES+=("$file")
283	  else
284	    DELETED_COUNT=$((DELETED_COUNT + 1))
285	  fi
286	done
287	REVIEW_FILES=("${EXISTING_FILES[@]}")
288	
289	if [ $DELETED_COUNT -gt 0 ]; then
290	  echo "Filtered $DELETED_COUNT deleted files from review scope"
291	fi
292	```
293	
294	3. **Deduplicate:** Remove duplicate paths (portable — bash 3.2+ compatible, handles spaces in paths)
295	
296	```bash
297	DEDUPED=()
298	while IFS= read -r line; do
299	  [ -n "$line" ] && DEDUPED+=("$line")
300	done < <(printf '%s\n' "${REVIEW_FILES[@]}" | sort -u)
301	REVIEW_FILES=("${DEDUPED[@]}")
302	```
303	
304	4. **Sort:** Alphabetical sort for reproducible agent input (already sorted by sort -u above)
305	
306	**Log final scope and warn if large:**
307	
308	```bash
309	if [ -n "$FILES_OVERRIDE" ]; then
310	  TIER="--files override"
311	elif [ -n "$SUMMARIES" ] && [ ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
312	  TIER="SUMMARY.md"
313	else
314	  TIER="git diff"
315	fi
316	echo "File scope: ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} files from ${TIER}"
317	
318	# Warn if file count is very large — may exceed agent context or produce superficial review
319	if [ ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} -gt 50 ]; then
320	  echo "Warning: ${#REVIEW_FILES[@]} files is a large review scope."
321	  echo "Consider using --files to narrow scope, or --depth=quick for a faster pass."
322	  if [ "$REVIEW_DEPTH" = "deep" ]; then
323	    echo "Switching from deep to standard depth for large file count."
324	    REVIEW_DEPTH="standard"
325	  fi
326	fi
327	```
328	
329	</step>
330	
331	<step name="check_empty_scope">
332	If REVIEW_FILES is empty:
333	```
334	No source files changed in phase ${PHASE_ARG}. Skipping review.
335	```
336	Exit workflow. Do NOT spawn agent or create REVIEW.md.
337	</step>
338	
339	<step name="structural_pre_pass">
340	Optional structural cross-module pass powered by fallow.
341	
342	Read fallow config gates:
343	
344	```bash
345	FALLOW_ENABLED=$(gsd_run query config-get code_quality.fallow.enabled 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
346	FALLOW_SCOPE=$(gsd_run query config-get code_quality.fallow.scope 2>/dev/null || echo "phase")
347	FALLOW_PROFILE=$(gsd_run query config-get code_quality.fallow.profile 2>/dev/null || echo "standard")
348	FALLOW_MCP=$(gsd_run query config-get code_quality.fallow.mcp 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
349	```
350	
351	Defaults are fail-closed and opt-in:
352	
353	- `enabled=false` (skip entirely)
354	- `scope=phase`
355	- `profile=standard`
356	- `mcp=false`
357	
358	When `FALLOW_ENABLED=true`:
359	
360	1. Resolve binary via PATH first, then `node_modules/.bin/fallow`.
361	
362	```bash
363	FALLOW_BIN=$(FALLOW_CWD="$(pwd)" node -e "
364	const { resolveFallowBinary } = require('./gsd-core/bin/lib/fallow-runner.cjs');
365	const resolved = resolveFallowBinary({ cwd: process.env.FALLOW_CWD });
366	if (resolved) process.stdout.write(resolved);
367	")
368	```
369	
370	2. If binary is missing, fail with actionable message:
371	
372	```bash
373	if [ -z \"$FALLOW_BIN\" ]; then
374	  echo \"Error: fallow is enabled but no binary was found.\"
375	  echo \"Install fallow via \`npm install -D fallow\` or \`cargo install fallow\`.\"
376	  # Exit workflow
377	fi
378	```
379	
380	3. Execute structural pass and persist JSON (bounded at 120s; on timeout, behaves as a fallow crash):
381	
382	```bash
383	FALLOW_JSON_PATH="${PHASE_DIR}/FALLOW.json"
384	FALLOW_STDERR_TMP=$(mktemp)
385	if [ \"$FALLOW_SCOPE\" = \"repo\" ]; then
386	  timeout 120 \"$FALLOW_BIN\" audit --json --profile \"$FALLOW_PROFILE\" > \"${FALLOW_JSON_PATH}.tmp\" 2>\"$FALLOW_STDERR_TMP\"
387	  FALLOW_EXIT=$?
388	else
389	  # phase scope: pass the already-computed review file set
390	  printf '%s\n' \"${REVIEW_FILES[@]}\" | timeout 120 \"$FALLOW_BIN\" audit --json --profile \"$FALLOW_PROFILE\" --stdin-files > \"${FALLOW_JSON_PATH}.tmp\" 2>\"$FALLOW_STDERR_TMP\"
391	  FALLOW_EXIT=$?
392	fi
393	if [ $FALLOW_EXIT -ne 0 ]; then
394	  FALLOW_STDERR_SUMMARY=$(head -5 \"$FALLOW_STDERR_TMP\")
395	  rm -f \"${FALLOW_JSON_PATH}.tmp\" \"$FALLOW_STDERR_TMP\"
396	  echo \"WARNING: fallow structural pre-pass failed: ${FALLOW_STDERR_SUMMARY}\"
397	  FALLOW_JSON_PATH=""
398	else
399	  mv \"${FALLOW_JSON_PATH}.tmp\" \"$FALLOW_JSON_PATH\"
400	  rm -f \"$FALLOW_STDERR_TMP\"
401	fi
402	```
403	
404	On any failure of the structural pre-pass (binary missing, non-zero exit, timeout, or JSON parse error), the workflow continues with no `<structural_findings>` injection; the reviewer agent receives a normal review request.
405	
406	4. Optional MCP bridge path (runtime-dependent):
407	
408	- If `FALLOW_MCP=true`, set reviewer input mode to MCP-backed structural findings.
409	- Otherwise pass static JSON findings from `FALLOW.json`.
410	
411	When disabled, set:
412	
413	```bash
414	FALLOW_JSON_PATH=""
415	```
416	
417	</step>
418	
419	<step name="spawn_reviewer">
420	Compute the review output path:
421	```bash
422	REVIEW_PATH="${PHASE_DIR}/${PADDED_PHASE}-REVIEW.md"
423	```
424	
425	Compute DIFF_BASE for agent context (in case agent needs it):
426	
427	```bash
428	PHASE_COMMITS=$(git log --oneline --all --grep="${PADDED_PHASE}" --format="%H" 2>/dev/null)
429	if [ -n "$PHASE_COMMITS" ]; then
430	  DIFF_BASE=$(echo "$PHASE_COMMITS" | tail -1)^
431	else
432	  DIFF_BASE=""
433	fi
434	```
435	
436	Build files_to_read block for agent:
437	
438	```bash
439	FILES_TO_READ=""
440	for file in "${REVIEW_FILES[@]}"; do
441	  FILES_TO_READ+="- ${file}\n"
442	done
443	```
444	
445	Build config block for agent:
446	
447	```bash
448	CONFIG_FILES=""
449	for file in "${REVIEW_FILES[@]}"; do
450	  CONFIG_FILES+="  - ${file}\n"
451	done
452	```
453	
454	Build structural findings block for agent:
455	
456	```bash
457	STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS_BLOCK=""
458	MAX_FINDINGS_SIZE=50000
459	if [ -n "$FALLOW_JSON_PATH" ] && [ -f "$FALLOW_JSON_PATH" ]; then
460	  FALLOW_JSON_SIZE=$(wc -c < "$FALLOW_JSON_PATH" | tr -d '[:space:]')
461	  if [ "$FALLOW_JSON_SIZE" -le "$MAX_FINDINGS_SIZE" ]; then
462	    # Escape any literal closing tag before embedding; the closing tag literal is escaped to prevent prompt-structure breakage if a fallow finding's file path or message contains the sequence.
463	    SAFE_FALLOW_JSON=$(sed 's#</structural_findings>#<\/structural_findings>#g' "$FALLOW_JSON_PATH")
464	    STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS_BLOCK=$(printf '<structural_findings>\n%s\n</structural_findings>\n' "$SAFE_FALLOW_JSON")
465	  else
466	    echo "Warning: skipping structural findings embed (${FALLOW_JSON_SIZE} bytes > ${MAX_FINDINGS_SIZE} bytes). Re-run with narrower scope/profile if needed."
467	  fi
468	fi
469	```
470	
471	Spawn the gsd-code-reviewer agent:
472	
473	Print: `◆ Spawning code reviewer... (runs in a subagent — no output until it returns, ~1–5 min; expected, not a freeze)`
474	
475	```
476	Agent(subagent_type="gsd-code-reviewer", prompt="
477	<files_to_read>
478	${FILES_TO_READ}
479	</files_to_read>
480	
481	${STRUCTURAL_FINDINGS_BLOCK}
482	
483	<config>
484	depth: ${REVIEW_DEPTH}
485	phase_dir: ${PHASE_DIR}
486	review_path: ${REVIEW_PATH}
487	${DIFF_BASE:+diff_base: ${DIFF_BASE}}
488	files:
489	${CONFIG_FILES}
490	</config>
491	
492	Review the listed source files at ${REVIEW_DEPTH} depth. Write findings to ${REVIEW_PATH}.
493	Do NOT commit the output — the orchestrator handles that.
494	")
495	```
496	
497	> **ORCHESTRATOR RULE — CODEX RUNTIME**: After calling Agent() above, stop working on this task immediately. Do not read more files, edit code, or run tests related to this task while the subagent is active. Wait for the subagent to return its result. This prevents duplicate work, conflicting edits, and wasted context. Only resume when the subagent result is available.
498	
499	**Agent failure handling:**
500	
501	If the Agent() call fails (agent error, timeout, or exception):
502	
503	```
504	Error: Code review agent failed: ${error_message}
505	
506	No REVIEW.md created. You can retry with /gsd-code-review ${PHASE_ARG} or check agent logs.
507	```
508	
509	Do NOT proceed to commit_review step. Do NOT create a partial or empty REVIEW.md. Exit workflow.
510	</step>
511	
512	<step name="commit_review">
513	After agent completes successfully, verify REVIEW.md was created and has valid structure:
514	
515	```bash
516	if [ -f "${REVIEW_PATH}" ]; then
517	  # Validate REVIEW.md has valid YAML frontmatter with status field
518	  HAS_STATUS=$(REVIEW_PATH="${REVIEW_PATH}" node -e "
519	    const fs = require('fs');
520	    const content = fs.readFileSync(process.env.REVIEW_PATH, 'utf-8');
521	    const match = content.match(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/);
522	    if (match && /status:/.test(match[1])) { console.log('valid'); } else { console.log('invalid'); }
523	  " 2>/dev/null)
524	
525	  if [ "$HAS_STATUS" = "valid" ]; then
526	    echo "REVIEW.md created at ${REVIEW_PATH}"
527	
528	    if [ "$COMMIT_DOCS" = "true" ]; then
529	      gsd_run query commit \
530	        "docs(${PADDED_PHASE}): add code review report" \
531	        --files "${REVIEW_PATH}"
532	    fi
533	  else
534	    echo "Warning: REVIEW.md exists but has invalid or missing frontmatter (no status field)."
535	    echo "Agent may have produced malformed output. Not committing. Review manually: ${REVIEW_PATH}"
536	  fi
537	else
538	  echo "Warning: Agent completed but REVIEW.md not found at ${REVIEW_PATH}. This may indicate an agent issue."
539	  echo "No REVIEW.md to commit. Please retry with /gsd-code-review ${PHASE_ARG}"
540	fi
541	```
542	
543	</step>
544	
545	<step name="dispatch_fix">
546	If the `--fix` flag was passed (`FIX_FLAG=true`), delegate to the `code-review-fix.md` workflow
547	to auto-apply findings from the REVIEW.md that was just written (or that already existed).
548	
549	This step runs AFTER `commit_review` so REVIEW.md is guaranteed to be on disk before the fixer
550	is invoked. If REVIEW.md was not created (agent failed, scope was empty, etc.), the `code-review-fix.md`
551	workflow handles the missing-review error and exits cleanly.
552	
553	```bash
554	if [ "$FIX_FLAG" = "true" ]; then
555	  echo ""
556	  echo "─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
557	  echo "  --fix: delegating to code-review-fix.md"
558	  echo "─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
559	  echo ""
560	
561	  # Build the fix sub-arguments: pass phase arg plus any --all/--auto flags
562	  FIX_ARGS="${PHASE_ARG}"
563	  if [ "$FIX_ALL" = "true" ]; then
564	    FIX_ARGS="${FIX_ARGS} --all"
565	  fi
566	  if [ "$FIX_AUTO" = "true" ]; then
567	    FIX_ARGS="${FIX_ARGS} --auto"
568	  fi
569	
570	  # Load and execute the code-review-fix workflow.
571	  # The fix workflow is the canonical implementation for all fix logic:
572	  # gsd-code-fixer agent dispatch, --auto iteration loop, REVIEW-FIX.md commit,
573	  # and result presentation. Do not duplicate that logic here.
574	  Workflow(workflow="gsd-core/workflows/code-review-fix.md", args="${FIX_ARGS}")
575	
576	  # Exit after fix workflow completes — present_results is for review-only output.
577	  # The fix workflow has its own present_results step.
578	  # Exit workflow.
579	fi
580	```
581	
582	If `FIX_FLAG` is false, skip this step entirely and proceed to `present_results`.
583	</step>
584	
585	<step name="present_results">
586	Read the REVIEW.md YAML frontmatter to extract finding counts.
587	
588	Extract frontmatter between `---` delimiters first to avoid matching values in the review body:
589	
590	```bash
591	# Extract only the YAML frontmatter block (between first two --- lines)
592	FRONTMATTER=$(REVIEW_PATH="${REVIEW_PATH}" node -e "
593	  const fs = require('fs');
594	  const content = fs.readFileSync(process.env.REVIEW_PATH, 'utf-8');
595	  const match = content.match(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/);
596	  if (match) process.stdout.write(match[1]);
597	" 2>/dev/null)
598	
599	# Parse fields from frontmatter only (not full file)
600	STATUS=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep "^status:" | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
601	FILES_REVIEWED=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep "^files_reviewed:" | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
602	CRITICAL=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep -E "^[[:space:]]*(critical|blocker):" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
603	WARNING=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep "warning:" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
604	INFO=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep "info:" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
605	TOTAL=$(echo "$FRONTMATTER" | grep "total:" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
606	```

622	    Warning:   ${WARNING}

674	If `--files` validation fails unexpectedly on macOS, install coreutils or use absolute paths.

```
## Verdict: issues_found — 0 Critical, 7 Warnings, 6 Info

The core D-01..D-05 security properties held under adversarial tracing: ownership scoping, no-oracle silent 2XX, advisory-lock-first ordering, refcount protection against share-recipient unpin attacks (the `@Unique(['userId','cid'])` constraint rules out refcount inflation). openapi.json matches the opaque DTO; the Grafana alert metric name matches `metrics.service.ts` and sibling conventions.

Key warnings:

- **WR-01** — `vault.service.ts:255`: `SELECT abs(hashtext($1))::bigint` applies `abs()` to int4 *before* casting; a CID hashing to INT_MIN raises "integer out of range" permanently, making that file undeletable. The comment is backwards — `pg_advisory_xact_lock` takes signed bigint, so `abs()` is the only failure mode it "fixes." Fix: `hashtext($1)::bigint`.
- **WR-02** — `ipfs.controller.ts:119-128`: upload compensation via `guardedUnpin` is a guaranteed no-op (the failed `recordPin` is why no row exists) → permanent Kubo pin leak (drift only reports, never cleans), and on CID dedupe it increments the cross-user *security* counter, firing the new Grafana alert on internal DB failures.
- **WR-03** — `pending-unpin.processor.ts:50-62`: drain unpins outbox CIDs without re-checking `pinned_cids` refcount; the D-13 "sub-second window" rationale doesn't cover a 5-minute-to-unbounded outbox window, and pin-migration flows re-pin existing CIDs by design. Data-loss class.
- **WR-05/WR-06** — backfill script: Kubo-snapshot-before-DB-query TOCTOU deletes quota rows for uploads landing in between (no `pinned_at` cutoff), and the query hardcodes `false::boolean AS "isByoUser"`, nullifying the documented D-09 defensive re-assert.
- **WR-07** — counting BYO advisory rows in the hosted refcount (D-07) lets a BYO share-recipient pin-block deletion of hosted ciphertext indefinitely — and IN-05 means the drift report will never surface it.
- **WR-04** — `driftOrphanedPinsTotal` is a Counter re-incremented for the same orphans every hour; should be a Gauge.

Info items: no-op unpins inflate `fileUnpins`, missing CID regex on `UnpinDto`, `recordUnpin` is now dead code, the `LocalProvider` factory is triplicated across modules, and the misleading `outboxRowInserted` flag.
```

```
# Phase 42: API Unpin Integrity Verification Report

**Phase Goal:** Close the unpin-path gaps in `apps/api`: verify caller owns a `pinned_cids(userId, cid)` row before unpinning, reference-count CIDs across users before issuing global Kubo `pin/rm`, delete the caller's row, and decrement quota so deletes stop leaking quota.
**Verified:** 2026-06-12
**Status:** human_needed
**Re-verification:** No — initial verification

---

## Goal Achievement

### Observable Truths

| # | Truth | Status | Evidence |
|---|-------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Caller ownership checked before any Kubo call | VERIFIED | `guardedUnpin` checks `pinnedCidRepo.findOne({ where: { userId, cid } })` and returns silently (no Kubo, no delete) when no row found — `vault.service.ts:261-268` |
| 2 | Cross-user attempt returns silent 2XX with audit telemetry | VERIFIED | No-row path returns void unconditionally; `metricsService.unpinCrossUserAttempts.inc()` + `logger.warn` only when cross-user CID row found — `vault.service.ts:263-268`. Controller returns constant `{ success: true }` for all outcomes — `ipfs.controller.ts:149-151` |
| 3 | CIDs reference-counted across ALL users before global Kubo pin/rm issued | VERIFIED | `COUNT(*)` query on `pinned_cids WHERE cid = ?` (no user filter, no BYO filter) — `vault.service.ts:275-280`. Kubo `pin/rm` only triggered when `refcount === 0` |
| 4 | Caller's pinned_cids row deleted inside transaction (row delete = quota decrement) | VERIFIED | `pinnedCidRepo.delete({ userId, cid })` inside `this.dataSource.transaction(...)` callback — `vault.service.ts:272`. The old `recordUnpin` is not called separately; the in-transaction delete is the quota decrement |
| 5 | Per-CID advisory xact lock is FIRST statement in transaction | VERIFIED | `SELECT abs(hashtext($1))::bigint AS h` then `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock($1)` as first two `manager.query` calls inside transaction callback — `vault.service.ts:255-258`. Advisory lock ordering test in `vault.service.spec.ts:988` asserts this by call-order |
| 6 | When refcount reaches zero, CID inserted into pending_unpins outbox in the SAME transaction; Kubo called post-commit best-effort | VERIFIED | orIgnore insert into `pending_unpins` sets `outboxRowInserted = true` inside transaction — `vault.service.ts:284-292`. Kubo `ipfsProvider.unpinFile` called AFTER `});` closing the transaction — `vault.service.ts:298-304`. Comment explicitly documents ordering |
| 7 | Web client fires fetchQuota() after local removeUsage() (D-12) | VERIFIED | `quotaStore.fetchQuota().catch((err) => logger.warn('quota reconcile failed', err))` as fire-and-forget directly after `removeUsage()` — `apps/web/src/services/delete.service.ts:21-22` |
| 8 | Upload compensation path routes through guardedUnpin (not raw unpinFile) with D-13 comment | VERIFIED | `this.vaultService.guardedUnpin(req.user.id, result.cid).catch(() => undefined)` at `ipfs.controller.ts:126`, preceded by D-13 race window comment at lines 122-125. `ipfsProvider.unpinFile` does not appear in the controller at all (grep returns 0 matches for `ipfsProvider.unpinFile` in controller) |
```

```
## Current Milestone: v1.1 IPFS Infrastructure

**Goal:** Make CipherBox more IPFS-native — replace delegated-ipfs.dev, migrate selected vault state to IPFS/IPNS, add BYO-IPFS server-relay support, and establish performance baselines.

**Target features:**

- Reliable IPNS resolution (replace delegated-ipfs.dev with self-hosted or alternative provider)
- Reduce database dependence where feasible — migrate vault crypto material to IPFS while retaining `folder_ipns`, shares, device approvals, quota tracking, and the DB fallback for `encryptedRootFolderKey` in v1.1
- Bring-your-own IPFS node support via server-relay flow (client-direct deferred to v1.2)
- Comprehensive performance baselines (API, client, IPFS/IPNS latency, end-to-end user journeys)

## Requirements

### Validated (Milestone 1 — Staging MVP)

- Web3Auth authentication (email, OAuth, magic link, external wallet) — v0.1
- Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption + ECIES key wrapping — v0.1
- IPFS file storage via Kubo with IPNS metadata — v0.1
- Full file/folder CRUD with 20-level hierarchy — v0.1
- File browser web UI with terminal aesthetic — v0.1
```

```
## Key Decisions

| Decision                                    | Rationale                                                  | Outcome |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Full-stack vertical build order             | Test features end-to-end as they're built                  | Good    |
| Web + cross-platform desktop for v1.0       | Complete user experience across all platforms              | Good    |
| TEE republishing required for v1.0          | Zero-downtime vault access guarantee                       | Good    |
| Core Kit MPC replaces PnP Modal             | Self-hosted identity provider, MFA foundation              | Good    |
| Per-file IPNS metadata split                | Decouple content updates from folder publishes             | Good    |
| AES-256-CTR for streaming media             | Byte-range decryption enables in-browser playback          | Good    |
| Optimistic concurrency via sequence numbers | Lightweight conflict detection without distributed locks   | Good    |
| FUSE-T SMB backend (not NFS)                | macOS NFS kernel bug blocked WRITE RPCs for new files      | Good    |
| Encrypted recycle bin on IPFS               | Client-side retention enforcement, CID unpinning on delete | Good    |
| SIWE wallet login with hashed identifiers   | Privacy-preserving auth, unified identity across methods   | Good    |
| Decimal phase numbering for insertions      | Clear insertion semantics without renumbering              | Good    |
```

87	## 1.5. Closed-Phase Gate (#3569)
88	
89	The init JSON includes `phase_status` — one of `Pending | Planned | In Progress | Executed | Complete | Needs Review`. `Complete` means the phase has all summaries AND a `VERIFICATION.md` with `status: passed`. Replanning a closed phase silently rewrites plan docs that no longer match the shipped code, so the workflow must hard-stop here unless the operator explicitly overrides.
90	
91	Parse `phase_status` from the init JSON, then:
92	
93	```bash
94	FORCE_REPLAN=false
95	if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--force([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
96	  FORCE_REPLAN=true
97	fi
98	
99	if [ "${phase_status}" = "Complete" ]; then
100	  if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--reviews([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
101	    # --reviews on a closed phase is never legitimate — concerns belong in a
102	    # new phase or issue against the closed phase's commits.
103	    cat <<EOF >&2
104	Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
105	/gsd-plan-phase --reviews cannot replan a closed phase. If the review surfaced
106	real concerns, open a follow-up phase or file an issue against the closed
107	phase's commits. There is no --force override for --reviews on a closed phase.
108	EOF
109	    exit 1
110	  fi
111	  if [ "$FORCE_REPLAN" != "true" ]; then
112	    cat <<EOF >&2
113	Phase ${phase_number} (${phase_name}) is already CLOSED (VERIFICATION status: passed).
114	Replanning a closed phase will overwrite plan docs that no longer match the
115	shipped code. If you intentionally want to replan over closed work, re-run
116	with: /gsd-plan-phase ${phase_number} --force
117	
118	Otherwise, to view what shipped, see: ${verification_path}
119	EOF
120	    exit 1
121	  fi
122	  # FORCE_REPLAN=true: continue, but emit a banner so the operator sees the
123	  # decision in the transcript and in any committed plan docs.
124	  echo "WARNING: Replanning CLOSED phase ${phase_number} under --force. Verify the closeout was wrong before committing new plan docs." >&2
125	fi
126	```
127	
128	The gate fires only on `Complete`. `Executed` and `Needs Review` are not gated — those states mean planning was finished but verification did not pass, and replanning is a legitimate next step.

Use this for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops. Replaces the deleted `/gsd-research-phase` command.

136	In research-only mode, two modifiers control behavior when `RESEARCH.md` already exists:
137	
138	- **`--research`** — force-refresh re-research without prompting. Re-spawns the researcher unconditionally and overwrites the existing RESEARCH.md. (This is the existing `--research` flag's standard "force re-research" semantics, reused here.)
139	- **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, do **not** spawn the researcher. Sets `VIEW_ONLY=true`. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If `RESEARCH.md` does not exist, error with a hint to drop `--view`.
140	
141	```bash
142	RESEARCH_ONLY=false
143	VIEW_ONLY=false
144	if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ --research-phase[[:space:]]+([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?) ]]; then
145	  RESEARCH_ONLY=true
146	  PHASE="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
147	fi
148	if $RESEARCH_ONLY && [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--view([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then
149	  VIEW_ONLY=true
150	fi
151	```
152	
153	**`--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>` — CLI override (#703).** When present, this value is the resolved granularity passed to the planner — it wins over any per-phase `granularities.<type>` config, top-level `granularity` config, or project defaults. The init JSON always includes a `granularity` field reflecting the resolved value; read it from there. Invalid values (anything other than `coarse`, `standard`, `fine`) cause an error at the CLI boundary.
154	
155	Set `TEXT_MODE=true` if `--text` is present in $ARGUMENTS OR `text_mode` from init JSON is `true`. When `TEXT_MODE` is active, replace every `AskUserQuestion` call with a plain-text numbered list and ask the user to type their choice number. This is required for Claude Code remote sessions (`/rc` mode) where TUI menus don't work through the Claude App.
156	
157	**MVP_MODE resolution.** Resolve `MVP_MODE` once via the centralized `phase.mvp-mode` query verb. Precedence (first hit wins): CLI flag → ROADMAP.md `**Mode:** mvp` → `workflow.mvp_mode` config → false. The verb is the single source of truth — do not re-implement the chain.
158	
159	```bash
160	MVP_FLAG_ARG=""
161	if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--mvp([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then MVP_FLAG_ARG="--cli-flag"; fi
162	if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ (^|[[:space:]])--tdd([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then TDD_MODE=true; fi
163	```
164	
165	Defer the `phase.mvp-mode` query until `PHASE` is finalized (after explicit argument parsing/fallback phase detection + validation). The verb returns `true|false`; full result also exposes `source` (`cli_flag` | `roadmap` | `config` | `none`) for diagnostics. Mode is **all-or-nothing per phase** (PRD decision Q1).
166	
167	**Walking Skeleton gate.** When `MVP_MODE=true` AND `phase_number == "01"` AND there are zero prior phase summaries (new project), the planner runs in **Walking Skeleton mode** (per PRD decision Q2 — new projects only). Detect with:
168	
169	```bash
170	WALKING_SKELETON=false
171	if [ "$MVP_MODE" = "true" ] && [ "$padded_phase" = "01" ]; then
172	  PRIOR_SUMMARIES=$(gsd_run query phases.list --pick summaries_total 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
173	  if [ "$PRIOR_SUMMARIES" = "0" ]; then WALKING_SKELETON=true; fi
174	fi
175	```
176	
177	When `WALKING_SKELETON=true`:
178	
179	- Planner is instructed to produce `SKELETON.md` in the phase directory alongside `PLAN.md`. The template lives at `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/gsd-core/references/skeleton-template.md` — the planner reads it when producing SKELETON.md (lazy; not loaded on non-skeleton runs).
180	- The plan must scaffold project + routing + one real DB read/write + one real UI interaction + dev deployment — the thinnest possible end-to-end working slice.
181	
182	**Interaction with `--prd <filepath>`.** `--mvp` and `--prd` compose. The PRD express path (Step 3.5) creates `CONTEXT.md` from the PRD file and continues to research; the Walking Skeleton gate fires independently from the conditions above. When both are active on Phase 1 of a new project, the planner receives `WALKING_SKELETON=true` and PRD-derived context simultaneously — the PRD informs _what the skeleton should prove_. No precedence is needed; the two signals are orthogonal. See [`references/mvp-concepts.md`](../references/mvp-concepts.md) for the broader interaction map.
183	
184	Extract express-path args from $ARGUMENTS: `PRD_FILE` (`--prd <filepath>`), `INGEST_PATH` (`--ingest <path-or-glob>`), and optional `INGEST_FORMAT` (`--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>`, default `auto`).

186	`--prd` and `--ingest` are mutually exclusive. If both are present, error and exit:

477	### 5.0. Research-Only Modifiers (`--view`, `--research`)

479	**Skip if:** `RESEARCH_ONLY` is `false`.
480	
481	Three branches in research-only mode (`--research-phase <N>`):
482	
483	1. **`--view`**: print `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, no spawn, exit. If `RESEARCH.md` is missing, error with: `--view requires an existing RESEARCH.md; drop --view to spawn the researcher.`
484	2. **`--research`** (force-refresh): re-spawn researcher unconditionally — fall through to "Spawn gsd-phase-researcher" below.
485	3. **Neither flag AND `has_research=true`:** auto-use the existing research and exit cleanly — do not prompt, do not re-spawn. Emit `RESEARCH.md already exists for Phase ${PHASE}, using it. To force-refresh, re-invoke with --research; to print, re-invoke with --view. Path: ${research_path}` then exit. The explicit-flag escape hatches cover any deviation; this matches §5.1's promptless auto-use of existing research, removing the §5.0/§5.1 inconsistency (#159).
486	
487	```bash
488	if [[ "$VIEW_ONLY" == "true" ]]; then
489	  [[ -f "$research_path" ]] || { echo "Error: --view requires an existing RESEARCH.md (Phase ${PHASE}). Drop --view to spawn the researcher."; exit 1; }
490	  cat "$research_path"; exit 0

754	## 5.7. Schema Push Detection Gate
755	
756	> Detects schema-relevant files in the phase scope and injects a mandatory `[BLOCKING]` schema push task into the plan. Prevents false-positive verification where build/types pass because TypeScript types come from config, not the live database.
757	
758	Check if any files in the phase scope match schema patterns:
759	
760	```bash
761	PHASE_SECTION=$(gsd_run query roadmap.get-phase "${PHASE}" --pick section 2>/dev/null)
762	```
763	
764	Scan `PHASE_SECTION`, `CONTEXT.md` (if loaded), and `RESEARCH.md` (if exists) for file paths matching these ORM patterns:
765	
766	| ORM         | File Patterns                                           |
767	| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
768	| Payload CMS | `src/collections/**/*.ts`, `src/globals/**/*.ts`        |
769	| Prisma      | `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/schema/*.prisma`        |
770	| Drizzle     | `drizzle/schema.ts`, `src/db/schema.ts`, `drizzle/*.ts` |
771	| Supabase    | `supabase/migrations/*.sql`                             |
772	| TypeORM     | `src/entities/**/*.ts`, `src/migrations/**/*.ts`        |
773	
774	Also check if any existing PLAN.md files for this phase already reference these file patterns in `files_modified`.
775	
776	**If schema-relevant files detected:**
777	
778	Set `SCHEMA_PUSH_REQUIRED=true` and `SCHEMA_ORM={detected_orm}`.
779	
780	Determine the push command for the detected ORM:
781	
782	| ORM         | Push Command                | Non-TTY Workaround                                       |
783	| ----------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
784	| Payload CMS | `npx payload migrate`       | `CI=true PAYLOAD_MIGRATING=true npx payload migrate`     |
785	| Prisma      | `npx prisma db push`        | `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (if destructive) |
786	| Drizzle     | `npx drizzle-kit push`      | `npx drizzle-kit push`                                   |
787	| Supabase    | `supabase db push`          | Set `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` env var                      |
788	| TypeORM     | `npx typeorm migration:run` | `npx typeorm migration:run -d src/data-source.ts`        |
789	
790	Inject the following into the planner prompt (step 8) as an additional constraint:
791	
792	```markdown
793	<schema_push_requirement>
794	**[BLOCKING] Schema Push Required**
795	
796	This phase modifies schema-relevant files ({detected_files}). The planner MUST include
797	a `[BLOCKING]` task that runs the database schema push command AFTER all schema file
798	modifications are complete but BEFORE verification.
799	
800	- ORM detected: {SCHEMA_ORM}
801	- Push command: {push_command}
802	- Non-TTY workaround: {env_hint}
803	- If push requires interactive prompts that cannot be suppressed, flag the task for
804	  manual intervention with `autonomous: false`
805	
806	This task is mandatory — the phase CANNOT pass verification without it. Build and
807	type checks will pass without the push (types come from config, not the live database),
808	creating a false-positive verification state.
809	</schema_push_requirement>
810	```
811	
812	Display: `Schema files detected ({SCHEMA_ORM}) — [BLOCKING] push task will be injected into plans`
813	
814	**If no schema-relevant files detected:** Skip silently to step 6.

1249	## 9b. Handle Phase Split Recommendation
1250	
1251	When the planner returns `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`, it means the phase's source items exceed the context budget for full-fidelity implementation. The planner proposes groupings.
1252	
1253	**Extract from planner return:**
1254	
1255	- Proposed sub-phases (e.g., "17a: processing core (D-01 to D-19)", "17b: billing + config UX (D-20 to D-27)")
1256	- Which source items (REQ-IDs, D-XX decisions, RESEARCH items) go in each sub-phase
1257	- Why the split is necessary (context cost estimate, file count)
1258	
1259	**Present to user:**
1260	
1261	```
1262	## Phase {X} exceeds context budget for full-fidelity implementation
1263	
1264	The planner found {N} source items that exceed the context budget when
1265	planned at full fidelity. Instead of reducing scope, we recommend splitting:
1266	
1267	**Option 1: Split into sub-phases**
1268	- Phase {X}a: {name} — {items} ({N} source items, ~{P}% context)
1269	- Phase {X}b: {name} — {items} ({M} source items, ~{Q}% context)
1270	
1271	**Option 2: Proceed anyway** (planner will attempt all, quality may degrade past 50% context)
1272	
1273	**Option 3: Prioritize** — you choose which items to implement now,
1274	rest become a follow-up phase
1275	```
1276	
1277	Use AskUserQuestion with these 3 options.
1278	
1279	**If "Split":** Use `/gsd-phase --insert` to create the sub-phases, then replan each.
1280	**If "Proceed":** Return to planner with instruction to attempt all items at full fidelity, accepting more plans/tasks.
1281	**If "Prioritize":** Use AskUserQuestion (multiSelect) to let user pick which items are "now" vs "later". Create CONTEXT.md for each sub-phase with the selected items.

Do not read more files, edit code, or run tests related to this task while the subagent is active. Wait for the subagent to return its result. This prevents duplicate work, conflicting edits, and wasted context. Only resume when the subagent result is available.
1482	
1483	After planner returns -> spawn checker again (step 10), increment iteration_count.
1484	
1485	**If iteration_count >= 3:**
1486	
1487	Display: `Max iterations reached. {N} issues remain:` + issue list
1488	
1489	Offer: 1) Force proceed, 2) Provide guidance and retry, 3) Abandon

1491	## 12.5. Plan Bounce (Optional External Refinement)
1492	
1493	**Skip if:** `--skip-bounce` flag, `--gaps` flag, or bounce is not activated.
1494	
1495	**Activation:** Bounce runs when `--bounce` flag is present OR `workflow.plan_bounce` config is `true`. The `--skip-bounce` flag always wins (disables bounce even if config enables it). The `--gaps` flag also disables bounce (gap-closure mode should not modify plans externally).
1496	
1497	**Prerequisites:** `workflow.plan_bounce_script` must be set to a valid script path. If bounce is activated but no script is configured, display warning and skip:
1498	
1499	```
1500	⚠ Plan bounce activated but no script configured.
1501	Set workflow.plan_bounce_script to the path of your refinement script.
1502	Skipping bounce step.
1503	```
1504	
1505	**Read pass count:**
1506	
1507	```bash
1508	BOUNCE_PASSES=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.plan_bounce_passes 2>/dev/null || echo "2")
1509	BOUNCE_SCRIPT=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.plan_bounce_script 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null || true)
1510	```
1511	
1512	Display banner:
1513	
1514	```
1515	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1516	 GSD ► BOUNCING PLANS (External Refinement)
1517	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1518	
1519	Script: ${BOUNCE_SCRIPT}
1520	Max passes: ${BOUNCE_PASSES}
1521	```
1522	
1523	**For each PLAN.md file in the phase directory:**
1524	
1525	1. **Backup:** Copy `*-PLAN.md` to `*-PLAN.pre-bounce.md`
1526	
1527	```bash
1528	cp "${PLAN_FILE}" "${PLAN_FILE%.md}.pre-bounce.md"
1529	```
1530	
1531	2. **Invoke bounce script:**
1532	
1533	```bash
1534	"${BOUNCE_SCRIPT}" "${PLAN_FILE}" "${BOUNCE_PASSES}"
1535	```
1536	
1537	3. **Validate bounced plan — YAML frontmatter integrity:**
1538	   After the script returns, check that the bounced file still has valid YAML frontmatter (opening and closing `---` delimiters with parseable content between them). If the bounced plan breaks YAML frontmatter validation, restore the original from the pre-bounce.md backup and continue to the next plan:
1539	
1540	```
1541	⚠ Bounced plan ${PLAN_FILE} has broken YAML frontmatter — restoring original from pre-bounce backup.
1542	```
1543	
1544	4. **Handle script failure:** If the bounce script exits non-zero, restore the original plan from the pre-bounce.md backup and continue to the next plan:
1545	
1546	```
1547	⚠ Bounce script failed for ${PLAN_FILE} (exit code ${EXIT_CODE}) — restoring original from pre-bounce backup.
1548	```
1549	
1550	**After all plans are bounced:**
1551	
1552	5. **Re-run plan checker on bounced plans:** Spawn gsd-plan-checker (same as step 10) on all modified plans. If a bounced plan fails the checker, restore original from its pre-bounce.md backup:
1553	
1554	```
1555	⚠ Bounced plan ${PLAN_FILE} failed checker validation — restoring original from pre-bounce backup.
1556	```
1557	
1558	6. **Commit surviving bounced plans:** If at least one plan survived both the frontmatter validation and the checker re-run, commit the changes:
1559	
1560	```bash
1561	gsd_run query commit "refactor(${padded_phase}): bounce plans through external refinement" --files "${PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md"
1562	```
1563	
1564	Display summary:
1565	
1566	```
1567	Plan bounce complete: {survived}/{total} plans refined
1568	```
1569	
1570	**Clean up:** Remove all `*-PLAN.pre-bounce.md` backup files after the bounce step completes (whether plans survived or were restored).
1571	
1572	## 13. Requirements Coverage Gate
1573	
1574	After plans pass the checker (or checker is skipped), verify that all phase requirements are covered by at least one plan.
1575	
1576	**Skip if:** `phase_req_ids` is null or TBD (no requirements mapped to this phase).
1577	
1578	**Step 1: Extract requirement IDs claimed by plans**
1579	
1580	```bash
1581	# Collect all requirement IDs from plan frontmatter
1582	PLAN_REQS=$(grep -h "requirements_addressed\|requirements:" ${PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[]' | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//' | sort -u)
1583	```
1584	
1585	**Step 2: Compare against phase requirements from ROADMAP**
1586	
1587	For each REQ-ID in `phase_req_ids`:
1588	
1589	- If REQ-ID appears in `PLAN_REQS` → covered ✓
1590	- If REQ-ID does NOT appear in any plan → uncovered ✗
1591	
1592	**Step 3: Check CONTEXT.md features against plan objectives**
1593	
1594	Read CONTEXT.md `<decisions>` section. Extract feature/capability names. Check each against plan `<objective>` blocks. Features not mentioned in any plan objective → potentially dropped.
1595	
1596	**Step 4: Report**
1597	
1598	If all requirements covered and no dropped features:
1599	
1600	```
1601	✓ Requirements coverage: {N}/{N} REQ-IDs covered by plans
1602	```
1603	
1604	→ Proceed to step 14.
1605	
1606	If gaps found:
1607	
1608	```
1609	## ⚠ Requirements Coverage Gap
1610	
1611	{M} of {N} phase requirements are not assigned to any plan:
1612	
1613	| REQ-ID | Description | Plans |
1614	|--------|-------------|-------|
1615	| {id} | {from REQUIREMENTS.md} | None |
1616	
1617	{K} CONTEXT.md features not found in plan objectives:
1618	- {feature_name} — described in CONTEXT.md but no plan covers it
1619	
1620	Options:
1621	1. Re-plan to include missing requirements (recommended)
1622	2. Move uncovered requirements to next phase
1623	3. Proceed anyway — accept coverage gaps
1624	```
1625	
1626	If `TEXT_MODE` is true, present as a plain-text numbered list (options already shown in the block above). Otherwise use AskUserQuestion to present the options.
1627	
1628	## 13a. Decision Coverage Gate
1629	
1630	After the requirements coverage gate passes, verify that every trackable
1631	decision captured by discuss-phase in CONTEXT.md `<decisions>` is referenced
1632	by at least one plan. This is the **translation gate** from issue #2492 —
1633	its job is to refuse to mark a phase planned when a discuss-phase decision
1634	silently dropped on the way into the plans.
1635	
1636	**Skip if** `workflow.context_coverage_gate` is explicitly set to `false`
1637	(absent key = enabled). Also skip if no CONTEXT.md exists for this phase
1638	(nothing to translate) or if its `<decisions>` block is empty.
1639	
1640	```bash
1641	GATE_CFG=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.context_coverage_gate 2>/dev/null || echo "true")
1642	if [ "$GATE_CFG" != "false" ]; then
1643	  GATE_RESULT=$(gsd_run query check.decision-coverage-plan "${PHASE_DIR}" "${CONTEXT_PATH}")
1644	  # BLOCKING: refuse to mark phase planned when a trackable decision is uncovered.
1645	  # `passed: true` covers both real-pass and skipped cases (gate disabled / no CONTEXT.md /
1646	  # no trackable decisions). Verify-phase counterpart deliberately omits this exit-1 — that
1647	  # gate is non-blocking by design (review finding F15).
1648	  echo "$GATE_RESULT" | jq -e '(.passed // .data.passed) == true' >/dev/null || {
1649	    echo "$GATE_RESULT" | jq -r '(.message // .data.message // "Decision coverage gate failed.")'
1650	    exit 1
1651	  }
1652	fi
1653	```
1654	
1655	The handler returns JSON:
1656	
1657	```json
1658	{
1659	  "passed": true,
1660	  "skipped": false,
1661	  "total": 2,
1662	  "covered": 2,
1663	  "uncovered": [{ "id": "D-01", "text": "...", "category": "..." }],
1664	  "message": "..."
1665	}
1666	```
1667	
1668	**If `passed` is true (or `skipped` is true):** Display
1669	`✓ Decision coverage: {M}/{N} CONTEXT.md decisions covered by plans` (or
1670	`(skipped — gate disabled)` / `(skipped — no decisions)`) and proceed to
1671	step 13b.
1672	
1673	**If `passed` is false:** Display the handler's `message` block. It already
1674	names each uncovered decision (`D-NN | category | text`) and tells the user
1675	what to do — cite the id in a relevant plan's `must_haves` / `truths`, or
1676	move the decision under `### Claude's Discretion` / tag it `[informational]`
1677	if it should not be tracked. Then offer:
1678	
1679	```text
1680	Options:
1681	1. Re-plan to cover missing decisions (recommended)
1682	2. Edit CONTEXT.md to mark dropped decisions as [informational] / Discretion
1683	3. Proceed anyway — accept the coverage gap
1684	```
1685	
1686	If `TEXT_MODE` is true, present as a plain-text numbered list. Otherwise use
1687	AskUserQuestion. Selecting "Proceed anyway" continues to step 13b but
1688	records the override in STATE.md so verify-phase can re-surface it.
1689	
1690	**Why this gate blocks:** failing here is cheap. The plans are the contract
1691	between discuss-phase and execute-phase; if a decision isn't visible in any
1692	plan, no executor will implement it. Catching that now beats discovering it
1693	after thousands of dollars of execution.
1694	
1695	## 13b. Record Planning Completion in STATE.md
1696	
1697	After plans pass all gates, record that planning is complete so STATE.md reflects the new phase status:
1698	
1699	```bash
1700	gsd_run query state.planned-phase --phase "${PHASE_NUMBER}" --name "${PHASE_NAME}" --plans "${PLAN_COUNT}"
1701	```
1702	
1703	This updates STATUS to "Ready to execute", sets the correct plan count, and timestamps Last Activity.
1704	
1705	## 13c. Annotate ROADMAP with Wave Dependencies and Cross-cutting Constraints
1706	
1707	After plans are finalized, annotate the ROADMAP.md plan list for this phase with:
1708	
1709	- **Wave dependency notes** — a bold header before each wave group ("Wave 2 _(blocked on Wave 1 completion)_")
1710	- **Cross-cutting constraints** — a "Cross-cutting constraints:" subsection listing `must_haves.truths` entries that appear in 2 or more plans
1711	
1712	This step is derived entirely from existing PLAN frontmatter — no extra LLM pass is required.
1713	
1714	```bash
1715	gsd_run query roadmap.annotate-dependencies "${PHASE_NUMBER}"
1716	```
1717	
1718	This operation is idempotent: if wave headers or cross-cutting constraints already exist in the ROADMAP phase section, the command returns without modifying the file. Skip this step if `plan_count` is 0.
1719	
1720	## 13d. Commit Plans if commit_docs is true
1721	
1722	If `commit_docs` is true (from the init JSON parsed in step 1), commit the generated plan artifacts (including any ROADMAP.md annotations from step 13c):
1723	
1724	```bash
1725	gsd_run query commit "docs(${PADDED_PHASE}): create phase plan" --files "${PHASE_DIR}"/*-PLAN.md .planning/STATE.md .planning/ROADMAP.md
1726	```
1727	
1728	This commits all PLAN.md files for the phase plus the updated STATE.md and ROADMAP.md to version-control the planning artifacts. Skip this step if `commit_docs` is false.
1729	
1730	## 13e. Post-Planning Gap Analysis
1731	
1732	After all plans are generated, committed, and the Requirements Coverage Gate (§13)
1733	has run, emit a single unified gap report covering both REQUIREMENTS.md and the
1734	CONTEXT.md `<decisions>` section. This is a **proactive, post-hoc report** — it
1735	does not block phase advancement and does not re-plan. It exists so that any
1736	requirement or decision that slipped through the per-plan checks is surfaced in
1737	one place before execution begins.
1738	
1739	**Skip if:** `workflow.post_planning_gaps` is `false`. Default is `true`.
1740	
1741	```bash
1742	POST_PLANNING_GAPS=$(gsd_run query config-get workflow.post_planning_gaps --default true 2>/dev/null || echo true)
1743	if [ "$POST_PLANNING_GAPS" = "true" ]; then
1744	  # Scope to this phase's mapped REQ-IDs (#447); null/TBD skips the requirements comparison (CONTEXT.md decisions still reported), mirroring §13.
1745	  gsd_run gap-analysis --phase-dir "${PHASE_DIR}" --phase-req-ids "$(gsd_run query init.plan-phase "$PHASE" --pick phase_req_ids 2>/dev/null || echo TBD)"
1746	fi
1747	```
1748	
1749	(`gsd-tools.cjs gap-analysis` reads `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md`, `${PHASE_DIR}/CONTEXT.md`,
1750	and `${PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md`, then prints a markdown table with one row per
1751	REQ-ID and D-ID. Word-boundary matching prevents `REQ-1` from being mistaken for
1752	`REQ-10`.)
1753	
1754	**Output format (deterministic; sorted REQUIREMENTS.md → CONTEXT.md, then natural
1755	sort within source):**
1756	
1757	```
1758	## Post-Planning Gap Analysis
1759	
1760	| Source | Item | Status |
1761	|--------|------|--------|
1762	| REQUIREMENTS.md | REQ-01 | ✓ Covered |
1763	| REQUIREMENTS.md | REQ-02 | ✗ Not covered |
1764	| CONTEXT.md | D-01 | ✓ Covered |
1765	| CONTEXT.md | D-02 | ✗ Not covered |
1766	
1767	⚠ N items not covered by any plan
1768	```
1769	
1770	**Skip-gracefully behavior:**
1771	
1772	- REQUIREMENTS.md missing → CONTEXT-only report.
1773	- CONTEXT.md missing → REQUIREMENTS-only report.
1774	- Both missing or `<decisions>` block missing → "No requirements or decisions to check" line, no error.
1775	
1776	This step is non-blocking. If items are reported as not covered, the user may
1777	re-run `/gsd-plan-phase --gaps` to add plans, or proceed to execute-phase as-is.
1778

1904	   Get-Process node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.StartTime -lt (Get-Date).AddHours(-1)} | Stop-Process -Force
1905	   ```
1906	3. **Clean up stale task directories:**
1907	   ```powershell
1908	   # Remove stale subagent task dirs (Claude Code never cleans these on crash)
1909	   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\tasks\*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1910	   ```
1911	4. **Reduce MCP server count:** Temporarily disable non-essential MCP servers in settings.json
1912	5. **Retry:** Restart Claude Code and run `/gsd-plan-phase` again
1913	
1914	If freezes persist, try `--skip-research` to reduce the agent chain from 3 to 2 agents:

```
The commit landed (the gsd-tools helper false-negative per project memory). The research file is committed at `cc64fb350`.

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Phase:** 43 - fuse-write-durability
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- The false-ack bug is at `read_ops.rs:791-848` (macOS/Linux) and `platform/windows/write_ops.rs:821-865` (Windows). The thread spawns inside the callback before `reply.ok()`, and `handle.cleanup()` deletes the temp file before the upload. No journal exists.
- The mkdir orphan bug is at `write_ops.rs:602-609` (macOS/Linux) and `platform/windows/write_ops.rs:193-218` (Windows). Both arms warn-and-continue on `PublishResult::Conflict` but never add the parent to `mutated_folders` — so the debounce queue has no entry to retry.
- Zero new crate dependencies are needed. `serde_json`, `hex`, `base64`, `zeroize`, `dirs`, and `std::fs::File::sync_all()` are all already present in the workspace.
- `std::fs::File::sync_all()` is the correct fsync barrier on all 3 platforms — it calls `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS. There is already one `file.sync_all()` call in the codebase (`file_handle.rs:207`).
- `merge_folder_children()` in `lib.rs:275-327` already implements the upsert-into-remote pattern the journal replay path needs for D-06.
- `tauri_plugin_notification` is already installed and has usage patterns in `tray/mod.rs:323-330` and `updater.rs:80` to copy for the park notification.

### File Created

`.planning/phases/43-fuse-write-durability/43-RESEARCH.md`

### Confidence Assessment

| Area | Level | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bug locations and anatomy | HIGH | Direct source reads at exact line numbers |
| Standard Stack | HIGH | All deps confirmed in Cargo.toml — no new deps |
| Architecture | HIGH | Based on direct reads of all integration points |
| Pitfalls | HIGH | Derived from reading the actual bug paths |

### Open Questions

1. **Journal directory injection:** sdk crate should not call Tauri APIs — journal dir path needs to be injected from `fuse/mod.rs` at mount time; `dirs::data_local_dir()` is the fallback in sdk itself.
2. **New channel variant vs UploadComplete reuse:** Recommend a `FsEvent` enum with `UploadComplete` and `MkdirConflict { parent_ino }` variants to avoid misuse of mismatched fields.
3. **Replay point:** `mount_filesystem()` after pre-populate is the right spot — key material is already available there.

### Ready for Planning

Research complete. Planner can now create PLAN.md files (3 separate plans per D-12: sdk-journal, fuser-wiring, winfsp-wiring).
```

**Regarding Dimension 8 — Nyquist:** VALIDATION.md frontmatter explicitly sets `nyquist_compliant: false`. Per the Dimension 8 check, this means the phase has not self-declared Nyquist compliance, but the check is whether the plans provide automated verify. Plan 43-01 (the TDD plan) has full automated coverage for all journal behaviors. Plans 02/03/04 use `cargo build` as their verify — this is compile verification only, not behavioral. Per Check 8a, the requirement is that tasks have an `<automated>` command OR a Wave 0 dependency. All tasks in 43-02/03/04 have `<automated>` commands (build commands), so 8a is technically satisfied.

Check 8c (sampling continuity): Plans 43-02 and 43-03 have 3 consecutive implementation tasks with build-only verify — no behavioral test. However these tasks are wiring integration code where no in-module unit tests exist for the FUSE callback layer (explicitly acknowledged in VALIDATION.md). The Plan 43-01 TDD tests cover the journal contract these tasks use. This is a domain constraint, not a planning failure.

One issue remains that is substantive:

**43-04 Task 1 verify command** is `cargo build -p cipherbox-fuse && cargo build -p cipherbox-desktop 2>/dev/null || cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. The `2>/dev/null || fallback` pattern suppresses errors from the first build and silently falls back. If `cipherbox-fuse` builds but `cipherbox-desktop` fails with an actual error, the `||` arm runs and succeeds, masking the failure. This is a WARNING-level verification reliability issue.

The command `cargo build -p cipherbox-fuse && cargo build -p cipherbox-desktop 2>/dev/null || cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` redirects stderr and falls back via `||`, meaning a `cipherbox-desktop` build failure would be swallowed if the fallback command succeeds.

- Fix: Replace with two separate commands or remove the `2>/dev/null ||` fallback — e.g. `cargo build -p cipherbox-fuse && cargo build --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.

```
## Open Questions

1. **Journal directory on Linux**
   - What we know: `dirs::data_local_dir()` returns `~/.local/share` on Linux; app-specific subdirectory would be `~/.local/share/com.cipherbox.desktop/cb-journal/`.
   - What's unclear: Whether the Tauri `app_data_dir()` resolver is accessible from `crates/sdk` (it requires an AppHandle) or whether `dirs::data_local_dir()` should be used instead in sdk, with the concrete path injected at mount time from `apps/desktop`.
   - Recommendation: Inject the journal dir path into `WriteQueue::new(path)` from the mount orchestrator (in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs`) — sdk never calls Tauri APIs directly.

2. **New channel variant for mkdir conflict vs reusing UploadComplete**
   - What we know: `UploadComplete` carries `ino, new_cid, parent_ino, old_file_cid, pruned_cids, write_generation` — none of these fields make sense for a mkdir conflict signal.
   - What's unclear: Whether to add a new enum variant to an existing channel enum or create a new `MkdirConflict` mpsc channel.
   - Recommendation: Add a `FsEvent` enum with `UploadComplete` and `MkdirConflict { parent_ino }` variants to the existing mpsc channel. Minimizes new channels while keeping types clear.

3. **Replay at mount vs at login**
   - What we know: `mount_filesystem()` in `fuse/mod.rs` runs after key material is available. The journal requires the public key for ECIES unwrapping on replay.
   - What's unclear: Whether replay belongs in `mount_filesystem()` or in an earlier auth step.
   - Recommendation: Replay in `mount_filesystem()` after the pre-populate step, since key material is already available there and the IPNS sequence numbers are already seeded.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `std::fs::File::sync_all()` | Journal fsync barrier | Yes (std) | rustc workspace | — |
| `serde_json` | Journal serialization | Yes | workspace | — |
| `tauri_plugin_notification` | Park notification | Yes | 2.x (Cargo.toml:24) | Log only |
| `dirs` crate | Journal dir path (sdk) | Yes | workspace 5.x | Inject path from Tauri AppHandle |
```

```
579	   - Recommendation: Inject the journal dir path into `WriteQueue::new(path)` from the mount orchestrator (in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs`) — sdk never calls Tauri APIs directly.

582	   - What we know: `UploadComplete` carries `ino, new_cid, parent_ino, old_file_cid, pruned_cids, write_generation` — none of these fields make sense for a mkdir conflict signal.
583	   - What's unclear: Whether to add a new enum variant to an existing channel enum or create a new `MkdirConflict` mpsc channel.

589	   - Recommendation: Replay in `mount_filesystem()` after the pre-populate step, since key material is already available there and the IPNS sequence numbers are already seeded.
```

111	Codex maps subagents to `spawn_agent`, which has no direct Codex mapping for Claude Code's `isolation="worktree"` parameter. Failing closed prevents main-checkout edits while the workflow believes agents are isolated.

113	If the project uses git submodules, worktree isolation is unsafe **only when a plan touches a submodule path** — the executor commit protocol cannot correctly handle submodule commits inside isolated worktrees. The previous behavior unconditionally disabled worktree isolation whenever `.gitmodules` existed, which penalised every plan in a submodule project even when the plan was nowhere near a submodule. Compute submodule paths once and intersect them per-plan with the plan's declared `files_modified` frontmatter.
114	
115	```bash
116	# Parse submodule paths from .gitmodules once (empty if no .gitmodules).
117	# SUBMODULE_PATHS is a newline-separated list of repo-relative paths.
118	if [ -f .gitmodules ]; then
119	  SUBMODULE_PATHS=$(git config --file .gitmodules --get-regexp '^submodule\..*\.path$' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}')
120	else
121	  SUBMODULE_PATHS=""
122	fi
123	```
124	
125	`SUBMODULE_PATHS` is exported to the `execute_waves` step, where the per-plan decision actually happens (see "Per-plan worktree decision" sub-step inside `execute_waves`). The decision is per-plan because different plans in the same wave can touch different files — only plans whose paths intersect a submodule must drop worktree isolation; plans nowhere near a submodule keep parallel isolation.

127	When `USE_WORKTREES` (project-level) is `false`, all executor agents run without `isolation="worktree"` — they execute sequentially on the main working tree instead of in parallel worktrees. The per-plan decision below has no effect when worktrees are project-disabled.

129	`USE_WORKTREES` is also automatically set to `false` for the duration of a run when `worktree base-check` detects that the orchestrator HEAD has diverged from the worktree fork base (the #683 condition — e.g. an unmerged milestone or feature branch). This check runs only when `RUNTIME=claude` because `isolation="worktree"` is a Claude Code-specific feature; other runtimes do not use it. The auto-degrade prints a one-line warning to stderr and falls through to the sequential path so executors do not hit the exit-42 worktree-branch-check halt. To restore parallel worktree execution, set `worktree.baseRef:"head"` in `.claude/settings.local.json` (or run `gsd-tools worktree set-baseref`) — this makes the fork base track the live HEAD instead of a fixed remote ref. The `worktree-branch-check` exit-42 guard inside each executor remains in place as a backstop.

245	
246	Interactive mode executes plans sequentially **inline** (no subagent spawning) with user
247	checkpoints between tasks. The user can review, modify, or redirect work at any point.
248	
249	**Interactive execution flow:**
250	
251	1. Load plan inventory as normal (discover_and_group_plans)
252	2. For each plan (sequentially, ignoring wave grouping):
253	
254	   a. **Present the plan to the user:**
255	
256	   ```
257	   ## Plan {plan_id}: {plan_name}
258	
259	   Objective: {from plan file}
260	   Tasks: {task_count}
261	
262	   Options:
263	   - Execute (proceed with all tasks)
264	   - Review first (show task breakdown before starting)
265	   - Skip (move to next plan)
266	   - Stop (end execution, save progress)
267	   ```
268	
269	   b. **If "Review first":** Read and display the full plan file. Ask again: Execute, Modify, Skip.
270	
271	   c. **If "Execute":** Read and follow `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/gsd-core/workflows/execute-plan.md` **inline**
272	   (do NOT spawn a subagent). Execute tasks one at a time.
273	
274	   d. **After each task:** Pause briefly. If the user intervenes (types anything), stop and address
275	   their feedback before continuing. Otherwise proceed to next task.
276	
277	   e. **After plan complete:** Show results, commit, create SUMMARY.md, then present next plan.
278	
279	3. After all plans: proceed to verification (same as normal mode).
280	
281	**Benefits of interactive mode:**
282	
283	- No subagent overhead — dramatically lower token usage
284	- User catches mistakes early — saves costly verification cycles
285	- Maintains GSD's planning/tracking structure
286	- Best for: small phases, bug fixes, verification gaps, learning GSD

291	<step name="handle_branching">
292	Check `branching_strategy` from init:
293	
294	**"none":** Skip, continue on current branch.

296	**"phase" or "milestone":** Use pre-computed `branch_name` from init.

298	Fork the new phase branch off `origin/HEAD` (the project's default branch), not the current HEAD — otherwise consecutive phases compound and stay unpushed (#2916). If `$BRANCH_NAME` already exists locally, reuse it as-is.
299	
300	```bash
301	DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')
302	DEFAULT_BRANCH=${DEFAULT_BRANCH:-main}
303	
304	if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH_NAME"; then
305	  git switch "$BRANCH_NAME" || { echo "ERROR: Could not switch to existing branch '$BRANCH_NAME'." >&2; exit 1; }
306	else
307	  if ! git fetch --quiet origin "$DEFAULT_BRANCH"; then  # #2916
308	    git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" \
309	      || { echo "ERROR: fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH failed and no local copy exists. Refusing to create '$BRANCH_NAME' off current HEAD (#2916)." >&2; exit 1; }
310	    echo "WARNING: fetch origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH failed; using local copy as base." >&2
311	  fi
312	  if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
313	    echo "WARNING: Uncommitted changes will be carried onto '$BRANCH_NAME' (branched off origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH, not previous HEAD)."
314	  else
315	    git switch --quiet "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null && git merge --ff-only --quiet "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
316	  fi
317	  # Pinned base + fail-fast: on success HEAD is exactly at origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH,
318	  # so a post-creation merge-base or "ahead-of" guard would be unreachable. The
319	  # explicit base argument here is the single source of correctness for #2916.
320	  git checkout -b "$BRANCH_NAME" "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH" \
321	    || { echo "ERROR: Could not create '$BRANCH_NAME' from origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH (#2916)." >&2; exit 1; }
322	fi
323	```

417	
418	   ```bash

437	   - Offer three choices:
438	     - **retry** — run the same plan through cross-AI again
