450	**Orchestrator cwd-drift guard (FIRST ACTION at execute_waves entry — #48):**
451	
452	A prior `Agent(isolation="worktree")` dispatch can silently leave the orchestrator's
453	cwd inside an agent worktree (or a subdirectory of one). Every subsequent
454	orchestrator-side git call would then target the wrong tree — this is how a wrong-base
455	merge nearly shipped ~1000 files. Resolve the _worktree root_ (so a subdirectory cwd
456	cannot skew the check) and refuse if it is an agent worktree. The discriminator is the
457	per-agent branch namespace `worktree-agent-*`, NOT the `.claude/worktrees/` path: the
458	orchestrator may itself be legitimately invoked from a feature worktree under
459	`.claude/worktrees/`, so a path-substring refusal would break legitimate runs. Do NOT
460	pin to `git worktree list`'s first entry — that is the main worktree, the wrong target
461	when the orchestrator legitimately runs from a feature worktree.
462	
463	```bash
464	ORCHESTRATOR_WT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || {
465	  echo "FATAL: execute_waves entry is not inside a git worktree (#48)." >&2; exit 1; }
466	ORCH_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)
467	if printf '%s' "$ORCH_BRANCH" | grep -Eq '^worktree-agent-'; then
468	  echo "FATAL: orchestrator cwd is inside an agent worktree (branch '$ORCH_BRANCH', root '$ORCHESTRATOR_WT') — refusing to execute waves (#48). A prior isolation=\"worktree\" dispatch drifted the cwd; re-run from the orchestrator's own worktree." >&2
469	  exit 1
470	fi
471	# Pin to the worktree root; each later orchestrator-side block re-pins the same way
472	# (see the #3174 cleanup guard). Treat $ORCHESTRATOR_WT as the canonical root for the
473	# rest of the phase — prefer `git -C "$ORCHESTRATOR_WT"` for cross-step git calls,
474	# since a bare `cd` does not persist across separate tool invocations.
475	export ORCHESTRATOR_WT
476	cd "$ORCHESTRATOR_WT" || { echo "FATAL: cannot cd to orchestrator worktree '$ORCHESTRATOR_WT' (#48)." >&2; exit 1; }
477	```
478	
479	**Stream-idle-timeout prevention — checkpoint heartbeats (#2410):**
480	
481	Multi-plan phases can accumulate enough subagent context that the Claude API
482	SSE layer terminates with `Stream idle timeout - partial response received`
483	between a large tool_result and the next assistant turn (seen on Claude Code
484	
485	- Opus 4.7 at ~200K+ cache_read). To keep the stream warm, emit short
486	  assistant-text heartbeats — **no tool call, just a literal line** — at every
487	  wave and plan boundary. Each heartbeat MUST start with `[checkpoint]` so
488	  tooling and `/gsd-manager`'s background-completion handler can grep partial
489	  transcripts. `{P}/{Q}` is the phase-wide completed/total plans counter and
490	  increases monotonically across waves. `{status}` is `complete` (success),
491	  `failed` (executor error), or `checkpoint` (human-gate returned).
492	
493	```
494	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} starting, {wave_plan_count} plan(s), {P}/{Q} plans done
495	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} plan {plan_id} starting ({P}/{Q} plans done)
496	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} plan {plan_id} {status} ({P}/{Q} plans done)
497	[checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} complete, {P}/{Q} plans done ({wave_success}/{wave_plan_count} ok)
498	```

509	   **Detection algorithm (pseudocode):**

511	   ```
512	   seen_files = {}
513	   overlapping_plans = []
514	   for each plan in wave_plans:
515	     for each file in plan.files_modified:
516	       if file in seen_files:
517	         overlapping_plans.add(plan, seen_files[file])  # both plans overlap on this file
518	       else:
519	         seen_files[file] = plan
520	   ```

795	rerun the same command. Do not fall back to broad worktree discovery.
796	
797	```bash
798	[ -n "${WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST:-}" ] && [ -f "$WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST" ] || {
799	  echo "BLOCKED: missing WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST; refusing broad worktree cleanup (#3384)." >&2
800	  exit 1
801	}
802	
803	# Guard: pin cleanup back to the orchestrator's OWN worktree and fail on branch drift (#3174, #630).
804	# Resolve from the dispatch-time orchestrator root persisted in the manifest — NOT `git worktree
805	# list`'s first entry, which is always the main checkout and would pin a non-primary (per-phase
806	# lane) orchestrator off its own branch, tripping the #3174 assertion below (#630). Byte-identical
807	# for a primary orchestrator (its root IS the first entry); the fallback covers pre-#630 manifests.
808	PRIMARY_WT=$(MANIFEST="$WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST" node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.MANIFEST,"utf8"));if(j&&j.orchestrator_root)process.stdout.write(String(j.orchestrator_root))}catch(e){}')
809	[ -n "$PRIMARY_WT" ] || PRIMARY_WT=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print substr($0,10); exit}')
810	if [ -z "$PRIMARY_WT" ]; then
811	  echo "FATAL: could not resolve orchestrator worktree before cleanup" >&2
812	  exit 1
813	fi
814	if [ -n "$PRIMARY_WT" ] && [ "$(pwd -P 2>/dev/null)" != "$(cd "$PRIMARY_WT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" ]; then echo "⚠ Orchestrator CWD drifted to $(pwd) — pinning to $PRIMARY_WT before worktree cleanup (#3174)"; cd "$PRIMARY_WT" || { echo "FATAL: cannot cd to primary worktree $PRIMARY_WT" >&2; exit 1; }; fi
815	ORCH_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
816	[ -z "${EXPECTED_BRANCH:-}" ] || [ "$ORCH_BRANCH" = "$EXPECTED_BRANCH" ] || { echo "FATAL: orchestrator on '$ORCH_BRANCH' but expected '$EXPECTED_BRANCH' before worktree cleanup — refusing to merge (#3174-class drift)" >&2; exit 1; }
817	
818	# Fail closed: SDK refusal (safety guard #3174/#3384) must surface — do not swallow exit 1.
819	gsd_run query worktree.cleanup-wave --manifest "$WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST" || exit 1
820	```
821	
822	**Cleanup-tail snippet (use after any wave whose merges did not flow through the templated path above):**
823	
824	If the orchestrator deviated from the standard wave merge path (e.g., custom inter-worktree base-update merges with `merge: bring …` style messages), run this snippet after the custom merges are complete. It reads only `WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST`; do not discover unrelated `worktree-agent-*` worktrees.
825	
826	```bash
827	# Cleanup-tail: pin orchestrator CWD to its OWN worktree before cleanup-tail (#3174, #630).
828	# Same fix as the templated path: resolve the dispatch-time orchestrator root from the manifest,
829	# not `git worktree list`'s first entry (always the main checkout — wrong for a lane orchestrator).
830	PRIMARY_WT=$(MANIFEST="$WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST" node -e 'const fs=require("fs");try{const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.MANIFEST,"utf8"));if(j&&j.orchestrator_root)process.stdout.write(String(j.orchestrator_root))}catch(e){}')
831	[ -n "$PRIMARY_WT" ] || PRIMARY_WT=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print substr($0,10); exit}')
832	if [ -n "$PRIMARY_WT" ] && [ "$(pwd -P 2>/dev/null)" != "$(cd "$PRIMARY_WT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" ]; then echo "⚠ Orchestrator CWD drifted to $(pwd) — pinning to $PRIMARY_WT before cleanup-tail (#3174)"; cd "$PRIMARY_WT" || { echo "FATAL: cannot cd to primary worktree $PRIMARY_WT" >&2; exit 1; }; fi
833	# Cleanup-tail: remove residual agent worktrees after a cross-wave-dependency deviation.
834	# Uses only the current wave manifest to avoid touching unrelated active agents (#3384).
835	WT_PATHS_FILE=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gsd-worktree-paths-XXXXXX")
836	node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p=process.env.WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST;try{if(!p)throw new Error("WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST is unset");if(!fs.existsSync(p))throw new Error("manifest does not exist");const s=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8");if(!s.trim())throw new Error("manifest is empty");const j=JSON.parse(s);for(const w of j.worktrees||[])if(w.worktree_path)console.log(w.worktree_path)}catch(e){console.error(`ERROR: cannot read worktree manifest ${p||"(unset)"}: ${e.message}`);process.exit(1)}' > "$WT_PATHS_FILE" || { echo "BLOCKED: cannot read WAVE_WORKTREE_MANIFEST; refusing cleanup (#3384)." >&2; exit 1; }
837	while IFS= read -r WT; do
838	  [ -z "$WT" ] && continue
839	  WT_BRANCH=$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null)
840	  [ -z "$WT_BRANCH" ] || [ "$WT_BRANCH" = "HEAD" ] && continue
841	  echo "Cleaning up residual worktree: $WT (branch: $WT_BRANCH)"
842	  git worktree unlock "$WT" 2>/dev/null || true
843	  if ! git worktree remove "$WT" --force; then
844	    WT_NAME=$(basename "$WT")
845	    if [ -f ".git/worktrees/${WT_NAME}/locked" ]; then
846	      echo "⚠ Worktree $WT is locked — unlock failed; manual cleanup required:"
847	      echo "    git worktree unlock \"$WT\" && git worktree remove \"$WT\" --force && git branch -D \"$WT_BRANCH\""
848	    else
849	      echo "⚠ Residual worktree at $WT — remove failed; manual cleanup required"
850	    fi
851	  else
852	    git branch -D "$WT_BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
853	  fi
854	done < "$WT_PATHS_FILE"
855	git worktree prune
856	```
857	
858	**When to skip step 5.5:**
859	
860	**If no plan in this wave used worktree isolation** (project-level `USE_WORKTREES=false` OR every plan in the wave had `USE_WORKTREES_FOR_PLAN=false` — i.e. `WAVE_WORKTREE_PLANS` from step 2.5 is empty): all agents ran on the main working tree — skip this step entirely.
861	
862	**If the orchestrator merged via custom messages (cross-wave-dependency deviation):** the templated cleanup loop above was not triggered for those merges. Run the cleanup-tail snippet above instead. After the snippet completes, proceed to step 5.6.
863	
864	**If at least one plan used worktrees but others did not:** still run this cleanup — it iterates over actual `git worktree list` output and only merges back the worktrees that were created, leaving sequential plans' commits on the main tree untouched.
865	
866	**If no worktrees found at runtime:** Skip silently — agents may have been spawned without worktree isolation, or the orchestrator already cleaned them up.
867	
868	5.6. **Post-merge build & test gate:**
869	
870	After merging all worktrees in a wave (parallel mode), or after the last plan completes
871	(serial mode), run a build and then the project's test suite to catch cross-plan
872	integration issues that individual worktree self-checks cannot detect (e.g., conflicting
873	type definitions, removed exports, import changes, link errors).
874	
875	This addresses the Generator self-evaluation blind spot identified in Anthropic's
876	harness engineering research: agents reliably report Self-Check: PASSED even when
877	merging their work creates failures.
878	
879	Read and execute `gsd-core/workflows/execute-phase/steps/post-merge-gate.md`.
880	
881	5.7. **Post-wave shared artifact update (when at least one plan used worktrees, skip if tests failed):**
882	
883	When **any** executor agent in this wave ran with `isolation="worktree"`, that agent skipped STATE.md and ROADMAP.md updates to avoid last-merge-wins overwrites. The orchestrator is the single writer for these files. After worktrees are merged back, update shared artifacts once for every completed plan in the wave (worktree-mode plans **and** sequential plans that ran on the main tree but deferred to the orchestrator for tracking writes).
884	
885	**Only update tracking when tests passed (TEST_EXIT=0).**
886	If tests failed or timed out, skip the tracking update — plans should
887	not be marked as complete when integration tests are failing or inconclusive.
888	
889	```bash
890	# Guard: only update tracking if post-merge tests passed
891	# Timeout (124) is treated as inconclusive — do NOT mark plans complete
892	if [ "${TEST_EXIT}" -eq 0 ]; then
893	  # Update ROADMAP plan progress for each completed plan in this wave
894	  for plan_id in {completed_plan_ids}; do
895	    gsd_run query roadmap.update-plan-progress "${PHASE_NUMBER}" "${plan_id}" "complete"
896	  done
897	
898	  # Only commit tracking files if they actually changed
899	  if ! git diff --quiet .planning/ROADMAP.md .planning/STATE.md 2>/dev/null; then
900	    gsd_run query commit "docs(phase-${PHASE_NUMBER}): update tracking after wave ${N}" --files .planning/ROADMAP.md .planning/STATE.md
901	  fi
902	elif [ "${TEST_EXIT}" -eq 124 ]; then
903	  echo "⚠ Skipping tracking update — test suite timed out. Plans remain in-progress. Run tests manually to confirm."
904	else
905	  echo "⚠ Skipping tracking update — post-merge tests failed (exit ${TEST_EXIT}). Plans remain in-progress until tests pass."
906	fi
907	```
908	
909	Where `WAVE_PLAN_IDS` is the space-separated list of plan IDs that completed in this wave.
910	
911	**If no plan in this wave used worktrees** (project-level `USE_WORKTREES=false` OR `WAVE_WORKTREE_PLANS` is empty): sequential agents already updated STATE.md and ROADMAP.md themselves — skip this step.
912	
913	5.8. **Handle test gate failures (when `WAVE_FAILURE_COUNT > 0`):**
914	
915	```
916	## ⚠ Post-Merge Test Failure (cumulative failures: ${WAVE_FAILURE_COUNT})
917	
918	Wave {N} worktrees merged successfully, but {M} tests fail after merge.
919	This typically indicates conflicting changes across parallel plans
920	(e.g., type definitions, shared imports, API contracts).
921	
922	Failed tests:
923	{first 10 lines of failure output}
924	
925	Options:
926	1. Fix now (recommended) — resolve conflicts before next wave
927	2. Continue — failures may compound in subsequent waves
928	```
929	
930	Note: If `WAVE_FAILURE_COUNT > 1`, strongly recommend "Fix now" — compounding
931	failures across multiple waves become exponentially harder to diagnose.
932	
933	If "Fix now": diagnose failures (typically import conflicts, missing types,
934	or changed function signatures from parallel plans modifying the same module).
935	Fix, commit as `fix: resolve post-merge conflicts from wave {N}`, re-run tests.
936	
937	**Why this matters:** Worktree isolation means each agent's Self-Check passes
938	in isolation. But when merged, add/add conflicts in shared files (models, registries,
939	CLI entry points) can silently drop code. The post-merge gate catches this before
940	the next wave builds on a broken foundation.
941	
942	6. **Report completion — spot-check claims first:**
943	
944	   **Wave-close heartbeat (#2410):** after spot-checks finish (pass or fail),
945	   before the `## Wave {N} Complete` summary, emit as a literal line:
946	
947	   ```
948	   [checkpoint] phase {PHASE_NUMBER} wave {N}/{M} complete, {P}/{Q} plans done ({wave_success}/{wave_plan_count} ok)
949	   ```
950	
951	   For each SUMMARY.md:
952	   - Verify first 2 files from `key-files.created` exist on disk
953	   - Check `git log --oneline --all --grep="{phase}-{plan}"` returns ≥1 commit
954	   - Check for `## Self-Check: FAILED` marker
955	
956	   If ANY spot-check fails: report which plan failed, route to failure handler — ask "Retry plan?" or "Continue with remaining waves?"
957	
958	   If pass:
959	
960	   ```
961	   ---
962	   ## Wave {N} Complete
963	
964	   **{Plan ID}: {Plan Name}**
965	   {What was built — from SUMMARY.md}
966	   {Notable deviations, if any}
967	
968	   {If more waves: what this enables for next wave}
969	   ---
970	   ```
971	
972	7. **Handle failures:**
973	   **Step 7.0 — classify before branching (#3095):**
974	   ```bash
975	   CLASS_JSON=$(gsd_run query agent.classify-failure -- "$AGENT_RETURN_BODY")
976	   CLASS=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.class')
977	   SENTINEL=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.sentinel // empty')
978	   RETRY_AFTER=$(echo "$CLASS_JSON" | jq -r '.retryAfterSeconds // empty')
979	   if [ -n "$RETRY_AFTER" ]; then RETRY_HINT="  Provider hinted retry-after: ${RETRY_AFTER}s"; else RETRY_HINT=""; fi
980	   ```
981	   One classifier branch handles sentinels across Claude/Copilot/Codex/Gemini. Reference: `docs/research/provider-rate-limit-signals.md`.
982	   **Step 7.1 — `class == "quota-exceeded"`:**
983	   Do not offer "retry now". Run step-5 spot-check first; if SUMMARY.md is missing but commits exist, route to safe-resume (`state.verify-against-disk`) instead of immediate redispatch.
984	   ```text
985	   ⚠ Plan {plan_id} terminated by provider quota / rate limit
986	     Runtime sentinel: {SENTINEL}
987	     {RETRY_HINT}
988	     Partial commits on worktree branch: {N}
989	     SUMMARY.md present: {yes|no}
990	     1. Wait for quota reset, then resume (recommended)
991	   2. Switch to a different runtime / model and resume
992	   3. Abort phase and report partial state
993	   ```
994	   Re-run `/gsd-execute-phase` after quota reset for Option 1.
995	   **Step 7.2 — `class == "classify-handoff-bug"`:**
996	   If error contains `classifyHandoffIfNeeded is not defined`, treat as Claude runtime bug. Run the same step-5 spot-checks; PASS => treat as success, FAIL => fall through.
997	   **Step 7.3 — `class == "unknown-failure"`:**
998	   Report failed plan and ask Continue/Stop; continuing may cascade into dependent plan failures.
999	
1000	7b. **Pre-wave dependency check (waves 2+ only):**
1001	Before wave N+1, run `gsd-tools.cjs query verify.key-links {phase_dir}/{plan}-PLAN.md` for each upcoming plan.
1002	If any PRIOR-wave artifact link fails, present: - `## Cross-Plan Wiring Gap` with plan/link/from/pattern rows - Options: investigate+fix before continue, or continue with cascade risk
1003	Skip key-links that reference files in the CURRENT (upcoming) wave. 8. **Execute checkpoint plans between waves** — see `<checkpoint_handling>`. 9. **Proceed to next wave.**
1004	</step>
1005	<step name="checkpoint_handling">
1006	Plans with `autonomous: false` require user interaction.
1007	**Auto-mode checkpoint handling:**
1008	Read auto-advance config (chain flag OR user preference — same boolean as `check.auto-mode`):
1009	
1010	```bash
1011	AUTO_MODE=$(gsd_run query check auto-mode --pick active 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
1012	```
1013	
1014	When executor returns a checkpoint AND `AUTO_MODE` is `true`:
1015	
1016	- **human-verify** → Auto-spawn continuation agent with `{user_response}` = `"approved"`. Log `⚡ Auto-approved checkpoint`.
1017	- **decision** → Auto-spawn continuation agent with `{user_response}` = first option from checkpoint details. Log `⚡ Auto-selected: [option]`.
1018	- **human-action** → Present to user (existing behavior below). Auth gates cannot be automated.
1019	
1020	**Standard flow (not auto-mode, or human-action type):**
1021	
1022	1. Spawn agent for checkpoint plan
1023	2. Agent runs until checkpoint task or auth gate → returns structured state
1024	3. Agent return includes: completed tasks table, current task + blocker, checkpoint type/details, what's awaited
1025	4. **Present to user:**
1026	
1027	   ```
1028	   ## Checkpoint: [Type]
1029	
1030	   **Plan:** 03-03 Dashboard Layout
1031	   **Progress:** 2/3 tasks complete
1032	
1033	   [Checkpoint Details from agent return]
1034	   [Awaiting section from agent return]
1035	   ```
1036	
1037	5. User responds: "approved"/"done" | issue description | decision selection
1038	6. **Spawn continuation agent (NOT resume)** using continuation-prompt.md template:
1039	   - `{completed_tasks_table}`: From checkpoint return
1040	   - `{resume_task_number}` + `{resume_task_name}`: Current task
1041	   - `{user_response}`: What user provided
1042	   - `{resume_instructions}`: Based on checkpoint type
1043	7. Continuation agent verifies previous commits, continues from resume point
1044	8. Repeat until plan completes or user stops
1045	
1046	**Why fresh agent, not resume:** Resume relies on internal serialization that breaks with parallel tool calls. Fresh agents with explicit state are more reliable.
1047	
1048	**Checkpoints in parallel waves:** Agent pauses and returns while other parallel agents may complete. Present checkpoint, spawn continuation, wait for all before next wave.
1049	</step>

1101	<step name="tdd_review_checkpoint">
1102	**Optional step — TDD collaborative review.**
1103	
1104	```bash

1106	```
1107	
1108	**Skip if `TDD_MODE` is `false`.**

1110	When `TDD_MODE` is `true`, check whether any completed plans in this phase have `type: tdd` in their frontmatter:
1111

1116	**If `TDD_PLANS` > 0:** Insert end-of-phase collaborative review checkpoint.
1117	
1118	1. Collect all SUMMARY.md files for TDD plans
1119	2. For each TDD plan summary, verify the RED/GREEN/REFACTOR gate sequence:
1120	   - RED gate: A failing test commit exists (`test(...)` commit with MUST-fail evidence)
1121	   - GREEN gate: An implementation commit exists (`feat(...)` commit making tests pass)
1122	   - REFACTOR gate: Optional cleanup commit (`refactor(...)` commit, tests still pass)
1123	3. If any TDD plan is missing the RED or GREEN gate commits, flag it:
1124	   ```
1125	   ⚠ TDD gate violation: Plan {plan_id} missing {RED|GREEN} phase commit.
1126	     Expected commit pattern: test({phase}-{plan}): ... → feat({phase}-{plan}): ...
1127	   ```
1128	4. Present collaborative review summary:
1129	
1130	   ```
1131	   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1132	    TDD REVIEW — Phase {X}
1133	   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1134	
1135	   TDD Plans: {TDD_PLANS} | Gate violations: {count}
1136	
1137	   | Plan | RED | GREEN | REFACTOR | Status |
1138	   |------|-----|-------|----------|--------|
1139	   | {id} |  ✓  |   ✓   |    ✓     | Pass   |
1140	   | {id} |  ✓  |   ✗   |    —     | FAIL   |
1141	   ```
1142	
1143	**Escalation under MVP+TDD.** When `MVP_MODE=true` AND `TDD_MODE=true`, the review verdict escalates from advisory to **blocking**: missing RED or GREEN gate commits prevent marking the phase complete.
1144	
1145	```text
1146	Phase blocked: {N} TDD plan(s) violate the RED→GREEN gate sequence under MVP+TDD.
1147	Resolve and re-run /gsd execute-phase, or override with
1148	/gsd execute-phase {phase} --force-mvp-gate to ship anyway.
1149	```
1150	
1151	`--force-mvp-gate` is the escape hatch (documented, not yet implemented). Policy is:
1152	
1153	- `MVP_MODE=true` AND `TDD_MODE=true`: violations are **blocking** unless explicitly overridden.
1154	- otherwise: violations are advisory/non-blocking and are surfaced for review.
1155	  The verifier agent (step `verify_phase_goal`) still checks TDD discipline in both cases.
1156	  </step>

24	HEAD_REF=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD || echo "DETACHED")

REVIEW.md written to `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.planning/phases/43-fuse-write-durability/43-REVIEW.md`. Status: **issues_found** — 8 critical, 9 warnings, 6 info. Not committed.

The journal write half (fsync-before-ack in `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs` and the happy-path ordering in both release paths) is correct. The replay/retry half is broken end-to-end:

**Critical findings:**

- **CR-01** `crates/fuse/src/lib.rs:1080-1101` — `fetch_merge_publish_parent` never publishes the parent IPNS record (no key in journal), yet returns `Ok` so the entry is removed without remote commit, **and unpins the CID the parent IPNS record still points to** — new data-loss risk; the UAT orphan bug is not actually fixed by replay.
- **CR-02** `lib.rs:1195-1227` — replay treats the journaled ECIES-**wrapped** file IPNS key as a raw 32-byte key: `try_into::<[u8;32]>` always fails, so every `UploadFile` replay with a key fails forever (and step 4 double-wraps the key).
- **CR-03** `write_ops.rs:525` / windows `:153` — mkdir journals the **TEE-wrapped** IPNS key (or `""`) into a field replayed as the user-wrapped `ipns_private_key_encrypted`; replayed folders become unpublishable.
- **CR-04** `read_ops.rs:956-964` — fuser release prepare failure (including journal fsync failure) falls through to `reply.ok()`: silent ack of a lost write, the exact bug the invariant exists to prevent.
- **CR-05** `platform/windows/write_ops.rs:748-751` — `UploadSpawnParams` references nonexistent `cipherbox_api_client::ApiConfig`, `crate::publish_coordinator::PublishCoordinator`, and `Arc<tokio::runtime::Runtime>` (fs has `Handle`): the `winfsp` feature cannot compile; "build clean" only covered default features.
- **CR-06** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/mod.rs` — Windows mount never calls `replay_for_vault`; the journal is write-only on Windows.
- **CR-07** — `record_failure` and `SyncStatus::WriteParked` have **zero production callers** (grep-verified): no retries, no parking, no tray/notification; the daemon's `WriteQueue::default()` points at a nonexistent temp dir.
- **CR-08** `read_ops.rs:941-943` — journal entry removed after ciphertext upload but before the debounced (unjournaled) parent-pointer publish; crash in that window orphans the file with nothing to replay.

**Key warnings:** replay order is `read_dir`-arbitrary (`created_at_ms` unused) so nested mkdirs/multi-writes can replay out of order; `resolve_folder_key` only handles depth-1 parents; journal file is chmod'd 0600 only after content lands and the parent dir is never fsynced; mkdir leaves a ghost inode on late prepare failure; full ciphertext base64-in-JSON means multi-GB allocations fsynced on the FUSE thread with no GC of parked/foreign-vault entries; replay blocks mount with no network timeouts.

## Verification Complete

**Status:** gaps_found

### Gaps Found — 8 blockers preventing goal achievement

**Group 1: Replay cannot complete a parent IPNS publish**

1. **CR-01 (D-06)** — `fetch_merge_publish_parent` (`lib.rs:1081-1101`) uploads merged metadata but never publishes the IPNS record (no parent IPNS private key in journal). Returns `Ok()`, so `journal.remove()` fires with no confirmed remote commit — the original orphan bug is not closed by replay. Additionally `unpin_content(&resolve.cid)` at line 1099 unpins the CID the parent IPNS record still points to, which can make the current parent folder unfetchable — new data-loss risk introduced by this phase.

2. **CR-02 (D-06)** — `replay_upload_entry` (`lib.rs:1224-1227`) casts the ECIES-wrapped file IPNS key (~117 bytes) directly to `[u8;32]` — always fails. No `UploadFile` entry with a key is ever replayed. Lines 1275-1282 also double-wrap an already-wrapped key.

3. **CR-03 (D-03)** — `write_ops.rs:525` and `windows/write_ops.rs:153` journal `encrypted_ipns_for_tee` (TEE-wrapped, or empty) as `child_ipns_key_hex`. `replay_mkdir_entry` writes this into `FolderEntry.ipns_private_key_encrypted` which everywhere else is the user-ECIES-wrapped key. After replay, the folder's IPNS key is either TEE-wrapped (client cannot unwrap) or empty — folder becomes permanently unpublishable.

**Group 2: Windows platform incomplete**

4. **CR-05 (D-12)** — `windows/write_ops.rs:748-751`: `UploadSpawnParams` declares `cipherbox_api_client::ApiConfig` (type doesn't exist; should be `ApiClient`), `Arc<tokio::runtime::Runtime>` (should be `tokio::runtime::Handle`), and `crate::publish_coordinator::PublishCoordinator` (module doesn't exist; `PublishCoordinator` is at crate root). The `winfsp` feature does not compile in the project's own code.

5. **CR-06 (D-12)** — `windows/mod.rs` constructs the journal and injects it into `CipherBoxFS` but never calls `replay_for_vault`. Windows journal is write-only — crashes are never recovered.

**Group 3: Retry/park/notification pipeline is dead code**

6. **CR-07 (D-09/D-10)** — `record_failure` is called only from unit tests. Background upload failure paths only `log::error!`. `SyncDaemon` (`sync.rs:64`) uses `WriteQueue::default()` pointing at `temp_dir/cipherbox-journal-default` (never created, wiped on reboot). `TrayStatus::WriteParked` and `send_write_parked_notification` are unreachable in production.

**Group 4: Ordering violations**

7. **CR-04 (D-04)** — `read_ops.rs:956-964`: the `Err` arm of `prepare_result` calls `handle.cleanup()` and falls through to `reply.ok()` at line 964. The OS is acked even when `journal.put` fails — silent data loss on disk-full / permission error / journal directory missing.

8. **CR-08 (D-08)** — `read_ops.rs:941-943` (and `windows/write_ops.rs:996-997`): journal entry removed after `upload_content` succeeds and `UploadComplete` is sent, but before the parent folder pointer is published via the debounced publisher (1.5s+ later). A crash in this window leaves an irrecoverable orphan with an empty journal. Entry is also removed when `publish_file_metadata` failed (only `log::warn`).

Structured gaps in VERIFICATION.md frontmatter for `/gsd-plan-phase --gaps`.

### Key architectural decision

Verified against `crates/crypto/src/hkdf.rs` and `crates/fuse/src/write_ops.rs`: **folder IPNS keys are randomly generated (`generate_ed25519_keypair`), not HKDF-derivable** — so re-derivation at replay is impossible for folders. ### Summary: All 8 Blockers Resolved

**CR-01** — VERIFIED. `fetch_merge_publish_parent` now signs and publishes the parent IPNS record using `ecies::unwrap_key` on the journaled `parent_ipns_key_hex`, returns `Err` on Conflict (entry retained), calls `record_publish` and unpins the OLD CID only on `Success`. (`lib.rs:1129-1183`)

**CR-02** — VERIFIED. `replay_upload_entry` calls `ecies::unwrap_key` before the `[u8;32]` cast (`lib.rs:1315`), stores journaled hex as-is without re-wrapping (`lib.rs:1398-1400`).

**CR-03** — VERIFIED. Both `write_ops.rs:529` and `windows/write_ops.rs:152` use `wrap_key(&ipns_private_key, &fs.public_key)` for `child_ipns_key_hex`. `replay_mkdir_entry` writes it directly into `FolderEntry.ipns_private_key_encrypted` (`lib.rs:1234`).

**CR-04** — VERIFIED. `read_ops.rs:1003` replies `reply.error(libc::EIO); return` — neither the `Ok` arm (line 992 explicit `return`) nor the `Err` arm fall through to the trailing `reply.ok()` at line 1010.

**CR-05** — VERIFIED. `windows/write_ops.rs:759-762`: `Arc<cipherbox_api_client::ApiClient>`, `tokio::runtime::Handle`, `Arc<crate::PublishCoordinator>`.

**CR-06** — VERIFIED. `windows/mod.rs:349-372`: `PublishCoordinator` seeded from `initial_sequences`, `cipherbox_fuse::replay_for_vault` called before `CipherBoxFS` construction.

**CR-07** — VERIFIED end-to-end. `record_failure` at `read_ops.rs:983` and `windows/write_ops.rs:1043`; `SyncDaemon` takes real `WriteQueue` from `commands/sync.rs:35-38` (`cb-journal` path); `sync_cycle` calls `load_all_for_vault` and emits `WriteParked` when `failed > 0`; bridge fires `send_write_parked_notification` with count-only neutral copy.

**CR-08 (fuser)** — VERIFIED. Fuser upload thread has no `journal.remove` at all — mechanism (b) per plan (`read_ops.rs:967-975`).

**CR-08 (Windows)** — WARNING (partial). Windows gates removal on per-file IPNS publish, not parent-pointer publish. For files without per-file IPNS key material, the entry is removed after `upload_content` alone, leaving the original orphan window. The fuser path is correct; Windows is a gate-behind-feature path. Fix: remove `spawn_journal.remove` from the Windows upload thread to match the fuser mechanism (b).

### Human Verification Required (5 items)

1. **Journal survival after SIGKILL** — crash/replay cycle requires live desktop + filesystem mount
2. **Park notification render** — requires live app and controlled network failure
3. **Mkdir orphan survival** — requires inducing a parent-publish conflict live
4. **Ciphertext-only journal check** — runtime confirmation of D-05 invariant
5. **Windows CR-08 orphan window** — Windows-specific test to determine if the partial CR-08 causes user-visible data loss for files without per-file IPNS keys

155	#### 4. Ciphertext-Only Journal
156	
157	**Test:** After creating a journal entry in a live session, open the cb-journal/*.json file.
158	**Expected:** Only base64/hex values (ciphertext, wrapped keys, IVs, IPNS names) — never readable file content or paths.
159	**Why human:** Requires creating a live journal entry. Static analysis confirms the D-05 invariant is enforced in the schema and tested (queue.rs:430-454), but runtime confirmation is prudent.
160	
161	#### 5. Windows CR-08 Orphan Window (Platform-Specific Check)
162	
163	**Test:** On Windows, copy a file that has no per-file IPNS key (any new file write), SIGKILL between `upload_content` success and the debounced parent-pointer publish, relaunch.
164	**Expected:** The file should be present in the vault after relaunch (replay should recover it). If it is not present, this confirms the residual orphan window identified in the WARNING above.
165	**Why human:** Requires Windows build, WinFsp mount, and controlled timing of SIGKILL. Cannot verify headlessly. This is specifically to assess whether the Windows CR-08 partial implementation causes user-visible data loss in practice.
166	
167	### WARNING: Windows CR-08 Partial Implementation
168	
169	The 43-06 plan chose mechanism (b) for the fuser path: remove the in-thread `journal.remove` entirely and let replay serve as the authoritative cleanup. The 43-07 plan directed using "the same mechanism chosen in 43-06" for Windows, but the Windows implementation instead chose a hybrid: gating removal on per-file IPNS publish success.
170	
171	**The residual window:** When a file lacks per-file IPNS key material (file_ipns_private_key, file_meta_ipns_name, or folder_key_for_file_meta is None), the `if let` pattern at `windows/write_ops.rs:1012` does not match, `file_meta_publish_ok` stays `true`, and the entry is removed immediately after `upload_content` succeeds — before the parent folder pointer is published by the debounced publisher. A crash in this window leaves the uploaded file with no parent metadata reference and no journal entry to drive replay.
172	
173	**Impact classification:** WARNING rather than BLOCKER because: (a) the fuser path (macOS/Linux) is fully correct; (b) Windows WinFsp is a gate-behind-feature platform not yet in production; (c) the window only applies to files without per-file IPNS keys, which is an edge case; (d) the improvement relative to the original bug is meaningful (upload-success window rather than nothing at all for files with per-file IPNS). However, for a complete Windows durability guarantee, this should be tracked.
174	
175	**To close:** Apply mechanism (b) to Windows: remove `spawn_journal.remove` from the upload thread entirely, matching `crates/fuse/src/read_ops.rs:967-975`.
176	
177	### Gaps Summary
178	
179	All eight round-1 blockers (CR-01..CR-08) are substantially resolved. The phase goal is achieved for the fuser (macOS/Linux) platform: writes are durable, replay correctly publishes parent IPNS records with the right keys, the error path replies EIO, and the park/notify pipeline is live end-to-end.
180	
181	One partial deviation exists on the Windows platform (CR-08): the journal entry is removed after per-file IPNS publish rather than after parent-pointer publish, leaving a residual orphan window for files without per-file IPNS keys. This does not block the phase from proceeding — Windows WinFsp support is a gate-behind-feature path, and the deviation is traceable with a clear fix. A follow-up fix or a targeted human test on Windows is recommended before shipping the Windows build.
182

## RESEARCH COMPLETE

**Phase:** 44 - ipns-conflict-handling
**Confidence:** HIGH

### Key Findings

- **Exact bug locations confirmed:** `folder/index.ts:204-232` — 2-attempt loop re-resolves seq only, republishes stale CID; `file/index.ts:225-231` — no CAS, full TOCTOU window.
- **Full caller sweep completed:** 18 call sites across `sdk/src/client.ts` (8), `sdk/src/bin/index.ts` (2), `sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (4), and `apps/web/src/hooks/` (4 more). Every site needs `baseChildren` added.
- **Existing merge helpers available:** `fetchAndDecryptMetadata` + `resolveIpnsRecord` already in `sdk-core`; `createAndPublishIpnsRecord` already takes `expectedSequenceNumber`; no new HTTP calls or packages needed.
- **Rust CAS path confirmed non-blocking:** `crates/fuse/src/lib.rs:326-439` already does re-fetch+merge on 409 (union merge, 1 retry). Different code path from TS; parity is correctly deferred.
- **ConflictError must live in `packages/sdk-core/src/errors.ts`** (not `packages/sdk`) because `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` throws it and `sdk-core` cannot import from `sdk`.
- **`batchPublishIpnsRecords` does NOT throw 409** — use `createAndPublishIpnsRecord` for file record CAS to get a detectable error signal.
- **`MAX_VERSIONS_PER_FILE`** is hardcoded at 10 in `sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:28` but Phase 39 made it user-configurable via vault settings; `updateFileMetadata` needs an optional `maxVersionsPerFile` param so conflict-resolution version merges honor user's configured limit.

### File Created

| Backoff values | LOW (assumed) | Reasoned from Rust analog; not a spec |

### Open Questions

1. Does `batchPublishIpnsRecords` batch response include per-record conflict signals in the body that the TS client currently ignores? (affects file CAS implementation strategy)
2. Should `maxVersionsPerFile` be a new param to `updateFileMetadata` or is the hardcoded 10 acceptable for the conflict path?

### Ready for Planning

Review complete. Wrote `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.planning/phases/44-ipns-conflict-handling/44-REVIEW.md` (not committed). 17 findings: 2 critical, 8 warnings, 7 info.

## Critical

**CR-01 — Merged children never returned to callers; next write silently overwrites remote children.** `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` (`packages/sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:197,230`) publishes the merged set on 409 but returns only `{ cid, newSequenceNumber }`. Every caller (client.ts x7, bin x2, shared-write x4, web hooks) commits its own pre-merge `updatedChildren` plus the fresh sequence number. The next local write then composes from the stale children with a *matching* seq — CAS passes, no 409, and the other writer's child is dropped from the authoritative record. For a `FolderEntry` that loses the wrapped subtree keys permanently. The phase fixes lost updates only for the single conflicting write and re-opens the hole one write later. Fix: return `publishedChildren` and have callers adopt it.

**CR-02 — `prunedCids` on the file 409 path can list CIDs still referenced by the published `versions[]`.** `packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:354` accumulates step-1 prunedCids without filtering against the final merged version list. Reachable when remote's versions list is shorter (concurrent `deleteVersion`, or differing `maxVersionsPerFile` across devices): `useFileOperations.ts:507` then unpins a CID the live metadata still references → version restore permanently broken. Fix: filter accumulated prunedCids against `{mergedMetadata.cid} ∪ mergedVersions` cids.

## Key warnings

- **WR-01:** `merge.ts:53-57` keeps local unconditionally on remote-delete (no `modifiedAt` check, asymmetric with local-delete) — every concurrent writer resurrects another device's deletes, producing ghost FilePointers referencing already-unenrolled IPNS names.
- **WR-02:** When remote wins a file conflict, the loser's `versions[]` (including the just-created base-content entry) is discarded — prior content silently vanishes from history.
- **WR-03:** Merge can yield duplicate names (local-add + remote-add, different ids) — breaks the unique-name invariant FUSE and all collision guards rely on.
- **WR-05:** `restoreVersion`/`deleteVersion` still publish file IPNS without `expectedSequenceNumber` — the TOCTOU window this phase closed remains open for version ops.
- **WR-06:** `updateFileMetadata` zeroizes the caller-owned key buffer in-place, undocumented in JSDoc — retry-wrapper footgun.
- **WR-08:** Conflict tests never assert the merged payload (the exact spot where CR-02/WR-02 hide).

## Verified clean

- All 16 `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call sites pass correct pre-mutation `baseChildren`; no post-mutation base anywhere.
- No caller uses the old `{ ipnsRecord }` return shape; no double-publish of file records remains.
- Non-409 errors rethrown immediately; backoff bounded (100ms·2^n capped 1500ms, jitter 0.5–1.0×); no infinite loop.
- Zero-knowledge holds: `ConflictError` and logs carry only IPNS names/sequence numbers.
- Confirmed server-side (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:171`) that batch CAS failures rethrow as HTTP 409, so `withConflictRetry` around `addFileToFolder` still functions.

## Verification Complete

**Status:** gaps_found
**Score:** 12/14 must-haves verified
**Report:** `.planning/phases/44-ipns-conflict-handling/44-VERIFICATION.md`

---

### Gaps Found — 2 blockers

**Gap 1 (CR-01 — Goal-defeating): Merged children not returned to callers**

`updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` publishes the merged children but returns only `{ cid, newSequenceNumber }` (`folder/index.ts:197,230`). Every caller then stores `updatedChildren` — the pre-merge local set — alongside the fresh sequence number:

- `client.ts:428-429` (createFolder): `parent.children = updatedChildren`
- `client.ts:514-515` (renameItem): `folder.children = updatedChildren`
- `client.ts:638-639` (deleteItem): `folder.children = updatedChildren`
- `client.ts:791-792` (uploadFile): `folder.children = updatedChildren`
- `shared-write.ts:226,362,390`: returns `{ updatedChildren, newSequenceNumber }` to web hook callers
- `useFileOperations.ts:467-468`: updates sequence only; store already set to `updatedChildren` at line 452

Consequence: device's next operation (rename, delete, second upload) composes from the stale `updatedChildren` and publishes with `expectedSequenceNumber = newSequenceNumber`. The CAS check passes — no 409 — and the remote-only children are silently overwritten. The lost-update bug is fixed only for the single write where the conflict fires; it re-opens on the next write.

Fix required: add `publishedChildren: FolderChild[]` to the return type and value; update all 14 call sites to adopt it.

**Gap 2 (CR-02 — Data integrity): prunedCids can list CIDs still referenced by published metadata**

`file/index.ts:263` computes initial `prunedCids` from the pre-conflict local version list. On 409, line 354 does `prunedCids = [...prunedCids, ...extraPruned]` without filtering against what `mergedMetadata.versions` actually references. A version that was pruned locally but re-added by the remote merge survives in `prunedCids` and is unpinned by `useFileOperations.ts:507-510`, permanently destroying that version's content.

Fix required: after building `mergedMetadata`, compute `referenced = new Set([mergedMetadata.cid, ...(mergedMetadata.versions ?? []).map(v => v.cid)])` and filter `prunedCids` against it before returning.

---

**What is correctly implemented (12/14):** ConflictError class, isConflictExhausted type-guard, mergeChildren with all 8 D-01 permutations + D-02 union fallback, the 4-attempt retry loop with re-fetch+decrypt+merge+re-encrypt+re-upload+CAS-publish+backoff, the file CAS publish (expectedSequenceNumber), loser-becomes-version logic, mergeVersions helper, maxVersionsPerFile param, all 14 SDK caller baseChildren sweeps, shared-write.ts file return shape rewire, web hook adoption (useFileOperations, useFileVersions), isConflictExhausted-gated logging.

Structured gaps in VERIFICATION.md frontmatter for `/gsd-plan-phase --gaps`.

  "content": "---\nname: project-cross-package-dist-staleness\ndescription: Downstream tsc typechecks against a dependency's BUILT dist, not its source — rebuild the dep package after public-API changes\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nIn the CipherBox monorepo, `@cipherbox/sdk` and `apps/web` typecheck against the **built dist** of their workspace dependencies (`@cipherbox/sdk-core`, `@cipherbox/sdk`), not the TypeScript source. After changing a dependency package's public API (e.g. adding a field to a function's return type), `pnpm --filter <consumer> exec tsc --noEmit` will report phantom errors (\"Property X does not exist\") until you rebuild the dependency's dist.\n\n**Why:** the packages publish `dist/index.d.ts` and consumers resolve types from there via package `exports`. Stale dist = stale types.\n\n**How to apply:** when a GSD plan changes sdk-core or sdk public types, the post-merge gate MUST run `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build` (and `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build` if sdk's surface changed) BEFORE running the consumer's `tsc`. This bit Phase 44 twice — wave 3 (sdk-core return-shape change) and gap wave 4 (shared-write `publishedChildren` threading into `useSharedWriteOps`). Both times the \"errors\" vanished after a dist rebuild. Encode the rebuild step into gap-plan verify chains explicitly. Related: [[project-roadmap-truncation-gsd-planner]].\n"
}

### What each phase delivered
- **42** — ownership-guarded `guardedUnpin` (per-CID advisory lock, cross-user refcounting, transactional quota decrement, `pending_unpins` outbox + drain worker, Grafana alert, non-BYO backfill). Verified against the live `cipherbox-postgres` schema.
- **43** — fsynced ciphertext-only write journal so `release()` no longer falsely acks; mkdir parent-publish conflicts now retry instead of orphaning; replay-on-mount across macOS/Linux (fuser) and Windows (WinFsp); park-notification pipeline. The first code review caught that the replay/retry half was broken end-to-end (8 criticals — wrong key wrapping, winfsp wouldn't compile, dead park pipeline); gap plans 43-05…08 closed them, plus one inline fix I applied to align Windows journal removal with the fuser replay-only mechanism.
- **44** — three-way folder merge on 409 (`mergeChildren`, union fallback, edit-beats-delete), 4-attempt backoff, typed `ConflictError`, file-record CAS with loser-becomes-version. Review caught two criticals that would have re-opened lost-updates one write later (`publishedChildren` not returned to callers) and unpinned live version CIDs; both closed and the merged-payload assertions the original tests lacked were added.

### Two things to know
1. **Phase 43 is not fully closed.** Its code is verified 18/18, but 4 behaviors genuinely need a live desktop + FUSE mount and can't be checked headlessly: journal survival after SIGKILL, park-notification render, mkdir-orphan survival, and a runtime ciphertext-only journal check. They're persisted in `43-UAT.md`; run `/gsd-verify-work 43` from a desktop session to close them. I left the phase `human_needed` rather than force-marking it Complete.
2. **I repaired a ROADMAP corruption.** The phase-44 gap planner truncated `.planning/ROADMAP.md` from 658 lines to 25 (lost phases 1–43), and it rode through several tracking commits before close-out caught it. I restored the full file from the last-good commit and re-applied only the legitimate Phase 44 gap-wave delta — now 663 lines, 29 phases, intact.   "content": "## Summary\n\nCloses the two unpin-path gaps from the v1.1 UAT audit (gap-closure Phase 42):\n\n- **Missing ownership check** — the IPFS unpin endpoint previously issued a global Kubo `pin/rm` for any CID the caller named, with no verification that the caller owned it. A share recipient (or any authenticated user who learned a CID) could unpin another user's content.\n- **Quota never decremented on unpin** — deletes leaked quota because the caller's `pinned_cids` row was never removed and usage never went down.\n\nBoth fixes land together so authorization, row deletion, and the quota update stay consistent.\n\n## What changed\n\n- **`VaultService.guardedUnpin`** — per-CID `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid))` serializes concurrent unpins; in one transaction it verifies the caller owns a `pinned_cids(userId, cid)` row, deletes it (the delete *is* the quota decrement), reference-counts the CID across **all** users, and inserts into a `pending_unpins` outbox only when the global refcount hits zero. Kubo `pin/rm` is issued post-commit, best-effort.\n- **No oracle for cross-user attempts** — unpinning a CID you don't own returns a silent `{ success: true }` and increments the audit metric `cipherbox_unpin_cross_user_attempts_total` (Grafana alert included). No 403 that would confirm a CID exists.\n- **`pending_unpins` outbox + drain worker** — a BullMQ processor drains the outbox (best-effort Kubo unpin) and a read-only drift report surfaces orphaned pins without mutating anything.\n- **Backfill** — one-shot non-BYO script restores honest quota for `pinned_cids` rows that predate this change.\n- **Web** — `delete.service` reconciles quota via `fetchQuota` after the local `removeUsage`.\n- Two TypeORM migrations (`AddPendingUnpins`, `AddPinnedCidCidIndex`), 3 new metrics, and the regenerated `@cipherbox/api-client` for the opaque unpin response DTO.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `gsd-verifier`: **passed**, 8/8 observable truths verified against the code.\n- Live DB schema confirmed against the `cipherbox-postgres` container: `pending_unpins` table + `idx_pending_unpins_cid` (unique) + `idx_pinned_cids_cid` all present with the expected column shape.\n- Targeted API suite green: 97/97 across `vault.service`, `ipfs.controller`, `pending-unpin`, `backfill-helpers` (TDD RED→GREEN for the guardedUnpin / processor / backfill plans).\n- Code review (advisory): 0 critical, 7 warnings, 6 info — see `.planning/phases/42-api-unpin-integrity/42-REVIEW.md`. None goal-defeating; worth a skim before merge (notably WR-01 `abs(hashtext)` cast ordering and WR-02 upload-compensation no-op).\n\n## Notes\n\n- Migrations and the regenerated `packages/api-client/` are committed alongside the API changes (pre-commit `check-api-client.sh` parity).\n- This is the base of a stacked series (Phase 42 → 43 → 44); 43 (FUSE write durability) and 44 (IPNS conflict handling) follow on their own branches.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n"

## Problem

Security review (REVIEW-2026-02-21-phase14.md) identified items deferred to future work:

- **M1**: `itemName` stored as plaintext on server. File/folder names in the `shares` table leak content metadata. Fix: encrypt `itemName` with recipient's public key; recipient decrypts for display.
- **M5**: `reWrapForRecipients` silently swallows errors. If key re-wrapping fails for a recipient, it logs a warning but the recipient gets a share with missing keys. Fix: surface a non-blocking notification to the sharer, or implement background retry.
- **L1**: `/shares/lookup` enables public key enumeration (200/404 distinction). Mitigated by requiring authentication and ThrottlerGuard, but an authenticated attacker can enumerate registered public keys. Consider returning 200 with `{ exists: boolean }` always.
- **L4**: No pagination on `getReceivedShares` and `getSentShares` endpoints. A user with many shares could see slow responses. Fix: add `limit`/`offset` query params.

## Solution

- M1: Encrypt `itemName` with recipient's public key (ECIES), decrypt client-side for display. Requires schema change (longer field for ciphertext).
- M5: Add a toast/notification system for background operation failures. Consider a retry queue in the share store.
- L1: Change lookup to always return 200 with `{ exists: boolean }` instead of 404. Update client to check boolean.
- L4: Add pagination with `@Query() limit: number, @Query() offset: number` with sensible defaults (limit=50, offset=0).

## Part A — Security findings

- **M1** (itemName plaintext): **OPEN** — still `varchar(255)` plaintext, no encrypted column anywhere. Column at `apps/api/src/shares/entities/share.entity.ts:45-50` (comment explicitly calls it plaintext); server stores raw `dto.itemName` at `apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:96`; client sends raw at `apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts:117` (contrast: `encryptedKey` IS ECIES-wrapped). Accepted privacy trade-off in `REVIEW-2026-02-21-phase14.md`. **Tracked in actionable queues: nowhere** (not in LOW-SEVERITY-BACKLOG.md or todos/pending; only in the Phase-14 review doc + BACKLOG snapshot).

- **M5** (reWrapForRecipients swallows errors): **IMPLEMENTED** (minor residual gaps) — now returns `Promise<{ failedRecipients: string[] }>` at `apps/web/src/services/share.service.ts:322`, collects failures at `:359-368`. Upload callers surface a warning toast (`apps/web/src/hooks/useFileOperations.ts:156-162` and `:314-321`); SDK emits `share:reWrapFailed` event (`packages/sdk/src/client.ts:138-148`). Gaps: the file-*update* caller at `useFileOperations.ts:492-497` ignores the returned `failedRecipients`, and no desktop subscriber consumes the SDK event. **Tracked: nowhere** (original finding closed).

- **L1** (/shares/lookup enumeration via 200/404): **IMPLEMENTED** — always returns 200 `{ exists: boolean }`. Service returns a bool with no `NotFoundException` (`apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts:291-300`); controller wraps as `{ exists }`, 400 only for malformed key (`apps/api/src/shares/shares.controller.ts:163-172`); response DTO is `{ exists: boolean }` only, no UUID leaked (`apps/api/src/shares/dto/lookup-user-response.dto.ts`). Residual: existence still probeable via the boolean itself, mitigated by auth + ThrottlerGuard. **Tracked: nowhere** (closed).

- **S1** (validate signedRecord vs DTO on publish): **OPEN** — publish only base64-decodes `dto.record` (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:60-65`) then stores it verbatim (`:247`, `:292`); embedded CID/sequence are never parsed/compared to `metadataCid`/`expectedSequenceNumber`. A parser (`ipns-record-parser.ts`) exists but is resolve-only, and even there it treats DB columns as authoritative and only warns on mismatch (`:545-549`). **Tracked in actionable queue: nowhere** — only as a row in BACKLOG.md:41 (status "Open") and source review `REVIEW-20260402-172126.md`; not in LOW-SEVERITY-BACKLOG.md or todos/pending.

- **S2** (signature verification skipped on missing fields / downgrade): **OPEN** — verification still gated on field presence. SDK-core throws on invalid sig but skips when fields absent (`packages/sdk-core/src/ipns/index.ts:197-219`); the web path is strictly weaker — only `logger.warn`s even when the signature is present and INVALID, still returning the CID (`apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts:177-205`). No caller checks `signatureVerified` (all 31 resolve call sites read only `.cid`/`.sequenceNumber`); the Rust client doesn't verify at all (`crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs`). **Tracked: nowhere actionable** — BACKLOG.md:42 ("Deferred") + source review only.

- **S3** (inconsistent private-key zeroization / no caller-owns-key convention): **OPEN/PARTIAL** — convention is still undocumented (not in any README/docs/Rust doc-comments) and zeroization remains mixed. TS: some paths `.fill(0)` generated keys (`packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:180`, `folder/index.ts:172-173`), others don't (`ipns/index.ts:39-98`, `folder/index.ts:186-279`, `vault/index.ts:32-52`); Phase 44 made `updateFileMetadata` zeroize a caller-passed key (`file/index.ts:401-403`) while its sibling `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` does not — an active contradiction. They live only in the security review and the stale `.planning/BACKLOG.md` snapshot, so nothing currently actions them.\n\n- **S1 (Medium) — publish does not validate `signedRecord` vs DTO fields.** On publish the server only base64-decodes `dto.record` (`apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts:60-65`) and stores it verbatim (`:247`, `:292`); the embedded CID/sequence inside the signed record are never parsed and compared against `metadataCid` / `expectedSequenceNumber`. A parser exists but is resolve-only and treats the DB columns as authoritative, only warning on mismatch.\n- **S2 (Medium) — signature verification is downgrade-able.** sdk-core throws on an invalid signature but skips verification entirely when fields are absent (`packages/sdk-core/src/ipns/index.ts:197-219`). The web path is weaker still — it only `logger.warn`s even when a present signature is INVALID and still returns the CID (`apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts:177-205`). No resolve caller checks `signatureVerified` (all call sites read only `.cid` / `.sequenceNumber`), and the Rust client does not verify at all (`crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs`).\n- **S3 (Medium) — inconsistent private-key zeroization; no caller-owns-key convention.** Some paths zeroize generated keys (`packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts:180`, `folder/index.ts:172-173`), others do not (`ipns/index.ts:39-98`, `vault/index.ts:32-52`). Phase 44 introduced an active contradiction: `updateFileMetadata` zeroizes a caller-passed key (`file/index.ts:401-403`) while its sibling `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` does not. Rust uses `Zeroizing`/`ZeroizeOnDrop` widely but several unwrap paths return raw `Vec<u8>` keys with inconsistent caller cleanup (`crates/crypto/src/ecies.rs:35-46`, `crates/fuse/src/lib.rs:993-1050`).\n\n## Solution\n\n- **S1**: On publish, parse the embedded CID + sequence from the signed record and reject (400) when they disagree with the DTO's `metadataCid` / `expectedSequenceNumber`.\n- **S2**: Once signed-record data is reliably populated, enforce verification: fail closed when a signature is present but invalid (web path must reject, not warn), have resolve callers honor `signatureVerified`, and add verification to the Rust client. Treat missing fields explicitly rather than silently skipping.\n- **S3**: Establish and document a caller-owns-key convention across the SDK (zeroize at the boundary that owns the buffer); reconcile the `updateFileMetadata` vs `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` contradiction; audit the Rust unwrap paths that return raw key bytes.\n"
}

## The reassuring answer first: nothing was lost

`gsd health` (W019) copied **both files verbatim** into `BACKLOG.md` on 2026-06-12 — I compared item-by-item: all of `DEFERRED.md` is `BACKLOG.md` lines 5–167, all of `REFACTORING.md` is lines 171–288, identical wording. So every deferred feature and improvement was already preserved in a living planning doc. The deletion only removed redundant copies.

## What I found and fixed — PR #486

Going through the contents surfaced that the BACKLOG snapshot (dated 2026-03-31) had drifted, so I reconciled it. A static codebase audit across phases 36–44 found:

**9 "open" items had actually shipped** — now marked done in BACKLOG with file/PR evidence, original tables kept as history:
- `folder.service.ts` + `bin.service.ts` retirement and the crypto→core circular-dep removal (Phase 38 / #422)
- User-configurable bin retention (Phase 39)
- Three-way folder merge (Phase 44 — the `mergeChildren` you just built)
- Security M5 and L1; refactors Tier-3 3.6 and 3.9

**4 security findings were genuinely open and tracked nowhere actionable** (only in stale review docs + the snapshot — exactly the "will get lost" case). I re-verified each against live code and promoted them to `todos/pending/`:
- **M1** — share `itemName` still plaintext at rest
- **S1/S2/S3** — IPNS publish doesn't validate `signedRecord` vs DTO; signature verification is downgrade-able; key zeroization is inconsistent (Phase 44 even introduced a `updateFileMetadata` vs `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` contradiction)

This landed as **PR #486** (`docs: reconcile backlog…`, 3 files, +84, MERGEABLE) on its own branch off `main` — it's pure planning hygiene, so I kept it out of the 42/43/44 feature stack.

## What I deliberately left in the backlog

The deferred **feature** set (sharing, desktop UI, MFA, performance) and the remaining **Tier-3 code-quality cleanups** (the `uint8ToBase64` dedup and ~11 others) stay in `BACKLOG.md`. They're correctly tracked there and not at risk of being lost — promoting all ~80 items to individual todos would just bury the actionable signal. I only escalated the security findings, which genuinely had no actionable home.

You've now got two PRs open: **#485** (Phase 42 feature + the husky/planning cleanup) and **#486** (this backlog reconciliation). Both target `main` and are independent.
